front: What is the overarching subject of Rule 1? Rule 1
back: The overarching subject of Rule 1 is the Conduct of the Game.

front: What are the dimensions of a regulation Canadian Amateur Tackle Football field, including the end zones? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 1
back: The field of play is 110 yards (100 metres) long by 65 yards (60 metres) wide. Additionally, there is a 20-yard (18.28 metres) long end zone at each end.

front: What is the 'Dead Line' according to the rules? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 1
back: The Dead Line is the line 20 yards (18.28 metres) behind each goal line and parallel to it.

front: Which line is considered part of the end zone? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 1
back: The goal line is considered part of the end zone.

front: How are the boundaries of the playing field defined, and are these lines in or out of bounds? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 2
back: The bounds are defined as the inside of the sidelines, end zone sidelines, and dead lines. These boundary lines are out of bounds.

front: From what point are all field dimension measurements taken? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 3
back: All measurements shall be taken from the inside edge of any boundary line.

front: How frequently must the field of play be marked by lines parallel to the goal line? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: The field of play shall be marked every 5 yards (metres) by lines parallel to the goal line.

front: Which specific yard lines must be marked with double thickness or double lines? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 5
back: The 35 and 45 yard (30 and 40 metre) lines shall be of double thickness or double lines.

front: Where are hash marks located on the field? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 6
back: Hash marks are located twenty-four yards (22 metres) from each sideline, marking each 5-yard (metre) stripe with a short cross stripe parallel to the sideline.

front: What type of markers are allowed at the intersections of goal lines, sidelines, dead lines, and end zone sidelines? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 8
back: Only flexible markers are allowed, specifically soft, flexible, four-sided pylons, 4” x 4” (10 cm x 10 cm) with an overall height of 18 inches (46 cm), and orange or red in colour.

front: Are the flexible markers placed at the intersections of lines considered inbounds or out of bounds? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 8
back: The flexible markers are considered inbounds.

front: What is the standard width between the vertical goal posts? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 9
back: The vertical goal posts shall be 18 feet 6 inches (5.64 metres) apart.

front: What is the required height of the crossbar's upper edge above the ground? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 9
back: The upper edge of the crossbar must be 10 feet (3.05 metres) above the ground.

front: What is the minimum required height for goal posts above ground level? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 9
back: The goal posts shall be at least 20 feet (6.1 metres) above the ground level, with new installations recommended to be 30 ft (9.1 metres).

front: Who is responsible for providing the mandatory padding for goal posts on a home field? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 9
back: It is the responsibility of the home team to provide the padding.

front: Are goal posts located on the goal line considered part of the end zone? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 9 Note
back: Yes, goal posts on the goal line are considered to be part of the end zone.

front: What is required if a non-regulation field has obstructions like running tracks? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 10
back: A clear set of boundary lines must be provided, at least 1 foot (0.3 metres) inside the track or obstruction.

front: What actions are defined as a 'play' in Canadian Amateur Tackle Football? Rule 1 | Section 1 | Article 11
back: A play is defined as any legally run scrimmage play (run, pass, kick), a convert attempt, or a kick-off, during both regulation time and overtime.

front: What material is required for the four-panel ball used in the game? Rule 1 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The ball must be made of pebbled grain leather.

front: What is the acceptable pressure range for the inflated rubber bladder of the game ball? Rule 1 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The pressure must be not less than 12 1/2 lbs. (85 kilopascals) and not more than 13 1/2 lbs (95 kpa).

front: What is the required shape of the game ball? Rule 1 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The game ball shall be in the shape of a prolate spheroid.

front: What are the acceptable circumference measurements for the long axis of the game ball? Rule 1 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The circumference of the long axis shall be from 27 3/4 to 28 1/2 inches (700 to 725 mm).

front: Who is responsible for providing the league-approved game ball(s)? Rule 1 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The Home Team shall provide a league approved ball or balls.

front: Who makes the final decision regarding the suitability of the game ball? Rule 1 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The decision of the Referee shall be final as to the suitability of the ball.

front: What color must the game ball be for day games? Rule 1 | Section 2 | Article 2
back: For day games, the ball shall be of a natural tan in colour.

front: Under what condition must the game ball's color be clearly visible? Rule 1 | Section 2 | Article 2
back: For night games, the ball must be of such colour as will make it clearly visible.

front: What is a restriction on the color of the game ball for both day and night games? Rule 1 | Section 2 | Article 2
back: In both day and night games, the colour of the ball shall, in no way, closely blend with the colour of the uniforms of the competing teams.

front: What is the standard length of a game in actual playing time for adults, and how is it divided? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: The game shall consist of 60 minutes of actual playing time, divided into 4 periods of 15 minutes each.

front: How long is a game for High School level players and below, and how is it divided? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: For players at the High School level or equivalent and below, the game shall consist of 48 minutes of actual playing time, divided into 4 periods of 12 minutes each.

front: Who declares first choice at the start of the first or second half at the start of the game? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: The captain of the visiting team, or the team winning the coin toss, shall declare whether to have first choice at the start of the first or second half.

front: What three options does the captain having first choice at the start of the first half have? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: The captain having first choice at the start of the first half has the option of 1. Kicking Off, 2. Receiving the kick off, or 3. Defending an end of the field.

front: When does the procedure for choosing kick off, receiving kick off, or end of field reverse? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: At the start of the 3rd period, the procedure shall be reversed. The team captain having the first choice for the 2nd half shall have the option of the 3 choices mentioned earlier, and the other captain the option of the remaining 1 or 2 choices.

front: After a touchdown, what choice does the captain of the team scored against have? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: After a touchdown, the captain of the team scored against shall have the choice of kicking off, or receiving the kick off.

front: When do teams change ends during a game? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: Teams shall change ends at the end of the 1st and 3rd periods.

front: How is the ball put into play at the start of the 2nd and 4th periods? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: At the start of the 2nd and 4th periods, the ball shall be put into play by the team entitled to do so, at a point corresponding exactly to the point where the ball became dead at the opposite end of the field, and in exactly the same manner as if play had not been interrupted by the end of the previous period.

front: How long is the standard rest period at half time? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: A 20-minute rest period shall be allowed at the end of the 2nd period, or such other rest period as the league shall decide.

front: What is the penalty if a team is late appearing on the field at the start of the 1st or 3rd period? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 5
back: The penalty for a team being late appearing on the field at the start of the 1st or 3rd period is L10, with no option.

front: What determines the procedure for breaking a tie game if the score is tied at the end of the 4th period? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 6
back: The procedure to break a tie game shall be the prerogative of the governing football association, with the consideration that the safety of the athlete is of prime importance. Any such procedures must be communicated in writing to both teams and the Referee prior to the game.

front: In the absence of prepared tie-breaking regulations, what options does the winner of the coin toss have for overtime? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 6
back: The winner of the coin toss shall choose one of the following options: 1) Offense or defense, with the offense at the opponent’s 35-yard line to start, or 2) Which end of the field shall be used for the overtime period.

front: In overtime, what happens after the loser of the toss exercises their option for the first extra period? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 6
back: The loser of the toss shall have the first choice of the two options (offense/defense or end of field) for subsequent even-numbered extra periods.

front: How long does each team retain the ball during an extra period in overtime? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 6
back: Each team retains the ball until it scores or fails to make a first down. The ball remains alive after a change of team possession until it is declared dead.

front: What is the scoring rule if a tie persists after three extra periods in overtime? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 6
back: If the score is still tied after three extra periods having been played, any subsequent touchdown must be followed by a two-point conversion.

front: Are team time-outs allowed during overtime play? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 6
back: No, there shall be no team time-outs during overtime play.

front: What is recommended regarding balls for wet day procedures? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 3 (Wet Day Procedure)
back: On wet days, it is recommended that at least three balls be available which may be changed at the discretion of the Referee.

front: What is suggested for keeping balls clean and dry on wet days? Rule 1 | Section 3 | Article 3 (Wet Day Procedure)
back: It is suggested that «ball persons» be used, one on either side of the field, to keep the balls as clean and dry as possible.

front: How many players from each team are allowed on the field at any one time? Rule 1 | Section 4 | Article 1
back: Each team consists of 12 players on the field at any one time.

front: What is the recommended minimum number of players a team should have dressed to start the game? Rule 1 | Section 4 | Article 1
back: It is recommended that Teams have a minimum of 24 players dressed to start the game.

front: How are teams designated for identification in Approved Rulings in the Case Book? Rule 1 | Section 4 | Article 2
back: The team which puts the ball into play shall be identified as Team A, and the other team as Team B.

front: Who is the sole communicator between a team and the officials? Rule 1 | Section 4 | Article 3
back: The captain shall be the sole communicator between the team and the officials, through the Referee.

front: What is the penalty for a player or bench occupant commenting for the supposed benefit of the officials? Rule 1 | Section 4 | Article 3
back: Penalty L10. No option.

front: Under what conditions can a choice made by a captain, such as on a kick off or penalty option, be revoked? Rule 1 | Section 4 | Article 3
back: After the choice on a kick off has been communicated to the opponents by the Referee, the choice may not be revoked. After the choice of penalty or option has been made, the choice may not be revoked.

front: When may the Referee decline a request for a measurement? Rule 1 | Section 4 | Article 3
back: The Referee may decline a request for a measurement if satisfied beyond all reasonable doubt that a first down has or has not been made.

front: Who is permitted in the vicinity of the measurement when the distance chains are called in? Rule 1 | Section 4 | Article 3
back: Only the on-field captain of each team shall be permitted in the vicinity of the measurement.

front: Under what circumstances does time start on the Referee's signal following a kick-off? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 1
back: Time starts on the Referee's signal when the ball, following a kick-off, touches, or is touched by a player of either team, in bounds.

front: When does time start if a 'time count' foul or a timeout due to crowd noise occurs? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 1
back: Time starts when the ball is snapped after a 'time count' foul or after a timeout due to the noise of the crowd.

front: After the 3-minute warning, when does time start following an incomplete forward pass or a ball carried out of bounds? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 1
back: After the 3-minute warning signal has been given in any half, time starts when the ball is snapped following an incomplete forward pass or the ball being carried out of bounds.

front: Can timing rules be amended by individual leagues, and if so, how? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 1
back: Yes, timing rules may be amended by individual leagues to shorten games into an allotted time slot, but no change may be made that will lengthen a game.

front: When does the game clock stop due to a procedural penalty after a timeout or 3-minute warning? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 2
back: The game clock stops (is held) following a timeout or after the 3-minute warning, if the game clock is already held from the previous play and the play is stopped for a procedural penalty by either Team.

front: When does time stop on the signal of a field official related to scoring? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 2
back: Time stops on the signal of a field official when a score has been made and throughout any convert attempt.

front: Under what condition does time stop if there are multiple player substitutions? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 2
back: Time stops if three or more players from either team substitute at the same time.

front: What happens to the game clock after the 3-minute warning in any half? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 2
back: Time stops when the ball becomes dead after the three-minute warning signal in any half.

front: When is it recommended that time stops in games shorter than 48 minutes? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 2
back: For any game of less than 48 minutes, it is recommended that time stops as the first down distance has been made (after the ball is dead).

front: What happens if the ball becomes dead with only a short period of time remaining in any period? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 3
back: The team in possession is entitled to one complete play, even if it extends beyond the normal termination of that period.

front: When does a period end if the last play is a legally scored touchdown? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 3
back: The period will be extended for the convert attempt following the touchdown, and will end when the ball is declared dead on the convert, without a foul.

front: How many timeouts is each team allowed per half, and for how long? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 4
back: Each team is entitled to two timeouts in each half, and each timeout is 1 minute long.

front: Who can request a timeout and during what timeframe? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 4
back: Any player, head coach, or designated head coach may request a timeout from the time the ball becomes dead until it is put into play.

front: What is the penalty if Team A players remain in close proximity to their bench after a timeout? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 4
back: Team A players will be penalized for illegal procedure (L5 PLS DR) if they remain in close proximity to their bench after a timeout and conference, instead of returning to their huddle or moving clearly away from the team bench area.

front: Under the mercy rule, when does the clock run continuously in the second half? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 5
back: Any time after the first half, if the difference in score between the two teams becomes 35 points or more, the clock will be running time for the remainder of the game.

front: What are the exceptions to the running clock under the mercy rule? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 5
back: The clock will stop for injuries, scores, timeouts, or any reason the Referee deems necessary to stop the clock.

front: Does the mercy rule apply to U Sport and CJFL levels? Rule 1 | Section 5 | Article 5
back: No, the mercy rule does not apply for U Sport and CJFL levels.

front: When is a player considered to be in possession of the ball? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 1
back: A player is in possession of the ball when it is firmly held in their hand or hands, arm or arms, leg or legs, or under their body.

front: When players from opposite teams dispute possession of the ball, who does it belong to? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 2
back: It shall belong to the player who first gained possession and has not lost possession.

front: If players of opposite teams legally gain simultaneous possession of the ball, to which team does the ball belong? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 3
back: It shall belong to the team which last previously had possession.

front: What happens if a forward pass is caught simultaneously by eligible receivers of both teams? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 3
back: The ball shall belong to Team A.

front: What happens if a kick-off is legally caught simultaneously by players of opposite teams before it has been touched by any other player after the kick-off? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 3
back: The kick-off is repeated at the previous line of kick-off.

front: What happens if a kick-off is legally caught simultaneously by players of opposite teams after it has been legally touched by another player or players? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 3
back: Possession goes to the team which last touched it before the simultaneous possession.

front: When does a change of possession occur during a scrimmage play? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 4
back: Team A is in possession until it loses possession (e.g., fumble, blocked kick). Team B is in possession when a B player gains possession. Until Team A or Team B gains possession, the ball is defined as a ".loose ball."

front: When does a change of possession occur during a forward pass? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 4
back: Team A is in possession until the pass is ruled incomplete, or the ball is intercepted by Team B. Team B is in possession when a B player intercepts the pass.

front: When does a change of possession occur during a scrimmage kick? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 4
back: Team A is in possession until the ball is kicked. Team B is in possession when a B player gains possession. Until Team B or Team A gains possession, the ball is ".in flight."

front: When does a change of possession occur during a return kick? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 4
back: Team B is in possession until the B player has kicked the ball, which is then ".in flight." until either Team A or Team B regains possession.

front: When does a change of possession occur during a kick-off? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 4
back: Neither team is in possession prior to the kick-off. Team B is in possession when a B player gains possession. Until Team B or Team A gains possession, the ball is ".in flight."

front: For penalty applications involving ".before change of possession, loose ball, ball in flight or after change of possession," when is legal touching of a kicked ball (other than a kickoff) considered possession? Rule 1 | Section 6 | Article 4
back: Such touching shall be deemed to be possession.

front: Under what conditions is the ball considered in play after a kick off or scrimmage? Rule 1 | Section 7 | Article 1
back: The ball is in play from a kick off or scrimmage until a field official stops play by sounding the whistle.

front: When does the ball remain in play after striking an official? Rule 1 | Section 7 | Article 1
back: The ball is in play when it strikes an official who is not out of bounds, except on a forward pass.

front: When is a ball held for a place kick considered in play? Rule 1 | Section 7 | Article 1
back: The ball is in play when it is held in position by a player for the purpose of making a place kick, except on a kick off.

front: What happens regarding play status if a forward pass is intercepted by a player in their end zone? Rule 1 | Section 7 | Article 1
back: The ball is in play if a forward pass is intercepted by a player in their end zone.

front: When may a play be stopped due to player injury or to impose a penalty? Rule 1 | Section 7 | Article 2
back: The play shall not be stopped because of player injury, or to impose a penalty until the ball is dead.

front: What is the penalty for an unauthorized delay due to player injury or any other reason? Rule 1 | Section 7 | Article 2
back: The penalty for unauthorized delay is L10, with no option.

front: What is the maximum duration for an official time out called by the Referee for medical attention related to bleeding? Rule 1 | Section 7 | Article 2
back: The Referee will call an official time out of no more than two (2) minutes to allow for medical attention and/or care of equipment related to bleeding.

front: When does the ball become dead during a game? Rule 1 | Section 8 | Article 1
back: The ball becomes dead when a field official blows the whistle to end play, the ball or a player with possession goes out of bounds, any score is made, the ball carrier is tackled and forward progress halted, a forward pass is incomplete or strikes certain objects/officials, it's in possession of a player lying on the ground (or held for a kick off), it strikes the opponent's goal post in flight from certain kicks (originating in field of play), or any part of the ball carrier (other than hands or feet) touches the ground.

front: Under what specific condition is the ball NOT dead even if a player's body part (other than hands or feet) touches the ground? Rule 1 | Section 8 | Article 1 (h) Exception
back: The ball is not dead when a player is holding the ball for a field goal or convert attempt, even if a part of their body other than hands or feet touches the ground.

front: When a ball carrier is tackled and driven back towards their own goal line, how is the point where the ball became dead determined? Rule 1 | Section 8 | Article 1 Note 1
back: The most forward point of advance is considered to be the point where the ball became dead.

front: If a ball carrier breaks a tackle and retreats toward their own goal line before being held, where is the point of advance for where the ball becomes dead? Rule 1 | Section 8 | Article 1 Note 2
back: The point of advance where the ball becomes dead is considered as the point at which the ball carrier is subsequently held.

front: What happens immediately if a ball carrier loses their helmet? Rule 1 | Section 8 | Article 1 (j)
back: The ball is immediately declared dead if the ball carrier loses their helmet.

front: What choices does a team in possession have if the whistle is inadvertently blown? Rule 1 | Section 8 | Article 1 Note 4 (1)
back: The team in possession has the choice to either cancel the current play and repeat it from where it began (PLS or kick-off), or have the play terminate at the PBH (Point of Ball Held) when the whistle was blown, with downs continuing if distance was not gained.

front: When is the ball considered to be in the End Zone? Rule 1 | Section 9 | Article 1
back: The ball is in the End Zone when: a) Any part of the ball is on, or behind the goal line, even in the air. b) Any part of the ball touches the plane of the goal line.

front: Under what condition is the ball NOT considered to be in the End Zone? Rule 1 | Section 9 | Article 1
back: The ball is not in the End Zone when the whole ball is completely ahead of the goal line, or the plane of the goal line.

front: Under what conditions is the ball considered out of bounds? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 1
back: The ball is out of bounds when: a) It touches any boundary line, or the ground or any object on or beyond these lines, including an official, any player or substitute. b) A player in possession of the ball touches any boundary line, or the ground or any object beyond these lines, except a field official or another player who is out of bounds, while the ball carrier is fully in bounds.

front: When the ball is carried out of bounds on the field of play, to which team does it belong? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 2
back: It shall belong to the team carrying it out of bounds, at the point where the ball crossed the line before it went out of bounds, except on third down when the required distance has not been gained.

front: Who gets possession when a ball is kicked out of bounds on the field of play? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 3
back: It shall belong to the opposite team, subject to the option of penalty applicable on the play.

front: What is the score when a player kicks a ball out of bounds in their own end zone? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 3
back: It will result in a score of 1 or 2 points, unless the ball is in the end zone from a forward pass intercepted in the end zone, or as a result of a fumble into the end zone by an opponent.

front: What happens to possession if a forward pass is thrown out of bounds? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 4
back: A ball thrown out of bounds on a forward pass shall remain in possession of the passing team, except on third down when the required distance has not been gained.

front: When a fumbled ball goes out of bounds, or touches a player and then goes out of bounds, which team gets possession? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 5
back: It shall belong to the team which last touched the ball, 24 yards (22 metres) in from the sideline at whichever point is closer to the goal line of the team entitled to possession, either where the ball went out of bounds, OR where the ball was last touched in the field of play. This excludes forward passes thrown out of bounds.

front: What is the ruling if a player fumbles the ball from the field of play directly over the opponent's goal line and out of bounds in the end zone without touching an opponent? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 6
back: It shall be ruled as a fumble, out of bounds, in the field of play, with the ball declared dead at the point where it was last touched in the field of play.

front: What is the ruling if a player fumbles the ball over the opponent's goal line, and it is last touched by a teammate without gaining possession and then goes out of bounds in the end zone? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 6
back: The ball shall be awarded to the team making the fumble, at the point of the original fumble.

front: What happens if a player fumbles the ball over the opponent's goal line, it's recovered or last touched by an opponent without possession, and then goes out of bounds in the end zone? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 6
back: There shall be no score and the ball shall be awarded to the opponent, at any point on or between the hash marks on the 20 yard (20 metre) line if the ball goes dead in the end zone. (Exception – Blocked Kick – Rule 5, Section 3, Article 4)

front: When is a safety touch awarded if a ball is fumbled or directed into a team's own end zone? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 6
back: A safety touch shall be awarded when a player fumbles or directs the ball from the field of play into their own end zone, where the ball goes out of bounds without possession being gained by either team.

front: What is the score when a player fumbles the ball in their own end zone to out of bounds in the end zone, even if touched by another player? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 7
back: A score of 1 or 2 points shall be awarded as applicable, unless the ball is in the end zone from a forward pass intercepted, or a fumble into the end zone by an opponent, or the ball carrier was knocked back and is not free to advance.

front: What is the penalty for an offside pass in the end zone when a player fumbles the ball from their own end zone, over the goal line, and then out of bounds without touching an opponent? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 7
back: Team A: 1st/2nd down results in a safety touch to B, or B's option to allow A to scrimmage 24 yards (22 metres) in from the out-of-bounds point with downs continuing. 3rd down results in a safety touch to B, or B's possession 24 yards (22 metres) in from the out-of-bounds point. Team B: 1 or 2 points as applicable, or A's option to allow B to scrimmage 24 yards (22 metres) in from the out-of-bounds point.

front: Under what conditions is a player allowed to go out of bounds and legally return to participate in the play? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 8
back: A player is allowed to return to the field and participate if they went out of bounds as a result of: a) a slippery field; b) contact with an opponent; or c) a missed block or tackle. The player must re-establish themselves in the field of play with at least one foot in bounds and no contact with out of bounds. Otherwise, it is illegal participation (Penalty – L10).

front: What is the penalty for an out-of-bounds player illegally reaching back into or re-entering the field of play to touch or recover a loose ball? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 8
back: Penalty – LB PF (Loss of Ball, Point of Foul).

front: What is the penalty if a player illegally participates by going out of bounds on a Kick-off before possession has been legally gained? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 8
back: Penalty - L10 from the point of kick-off repeat kick-off or option.

front: What is the penalty if a player illegally participates by going out of bounds after possession has been legally gained on a Kick-off? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 8
back: Penalty - L10 PP (Previous Play), PBH (Point Behind Hole), PBD (Point Ball Dead) or option.

front: What is the penalty if a player of Team B reaches back into the field of play while still out of bounds and touches a kickoff? Rule 1 | Section 10 | Article 8
back: Ball is dead at spot of touch with possession awarded along with 10-yard penalty for Illegal participation.

front: Under what condition may a Referee remove a player due to equipment? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 1
back: The Referee may remove any player from the game who is wearing equipment which, in the Referee’s opinion, endangers a participant.

front: What is illegal regarding team uniforms? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 1
back: No team shall wear uniforms that blend closely with the color of the ball. Numbers on uniforms must also be easy to identify.

front: What is the prime responsibility for proper equipment? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 1
back: The prime responsibility of proper equipment rests on the Head Coach or their designate.

front: What are the mandatory equipment items that all players must wear? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 1
back: All players must wear knee protection (soft padding or designed inserts without buckles, Velcro, clips, or straps), thigh guards, hip pads with tailbone protector, shoulder pads, a mouthguard covering all upper jaw teeth, and shoes meeting specific criteria or providing less ground fixation (like ripple soles or broomball type shoes without cleats).

front: What is prohibited regarding adhesive material, grease, or slippery substances? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 1
back: Adhesive material, grease, or any other slippery substance applied on a player’s person or clothing that affects the ball or an opponent is illegal.

front: What type of gloves are illegal? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 1
back: Any gloves which have any type of webbing between the digits are illegal.

front: What is the penalty for wearing illegal equipment (General a), b), f), g))? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 1
back: The offending player shall be removed from the game until the illegal equipment is replaced or the score sheet is corrected.

front: What is the penalty for violating mandatory equipment requirements (c))? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 1
back: Loss of 5 yards from the point where the ball would have been put into play, or added to another penalty. The offending player is removed until illegal equipment is replaced. Immediate substitution is made without delay. If multiple players offend on the same play, only 1 penalty L5 is applied per play.

front: What is the penalty for illegal adhesive materials, slippery substances, or gloves with webbing (d), e))? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 1
back: For Team A: 1st/2nd down - Loss of 10 yards, Down Repeated (L10 DR); 3rd down - Loss of 10 yards, Down Not Gained (L10, DNG-LB PBD). For Team B: Loss of 10 yards, Play Last Scrimmage (L10 PLS). The offending player is removed until the illegal item is removed. Immediate substitution is made without delay. If multiple players offend on the same play, only 1 penalty L10 is applied per play.

front: What type of helmets and facemasks are permitted? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 2
back: Only helmets and facemasks approved by the National Operating Committee on Safety in Athletic Equipment (NOCSAE) shall be worn by players.

front: What is the requirement for visors? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 2
back: All visors must be clear, not tinted, and no medical exceptions are allowed.

front: When must a player wear their helmet? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 2
back: A player shall be required to wear the helmet while in bounds and shall not voluntarily remove it while the play is in progress.

front: What is the penalty for violating helmet and facemask rules (a, b, c, d)? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 2
back: The offending player shall be removed from the game until the situation is corrected, and the offending team is assessed a 10-yard penalty PBD.

front: What happens if a player's helmet involuntarily comes off during play, not as a result of a foul? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 2
back: The player shall be required to leave the game for 3 plays.

front: What must a player do if they lose their helmet during play? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 2
back: The player must stop participating in the play.

front: What is the penalty for a player who loses their helmet and continues to participate in the play? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 2
back: Loss of 10 yards Play Before Dead Ball (PBD) or Play Before Holding (PBH).

front: How is hitting a player who has lost their helmet ruled? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 2
back: Unnecessary Roughness.

front: What type of mouthguard is required? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 3
back: A player shall wear an intra-oral mouth and tooth protector, which includes an occlusial portion and an optional labial portion. It is recommended to be custom-fitted or fitted by impressing teeth into it.

front: What is the penalty for a first infraction of not wearing a mouthguard properly? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 3
back: The Referee shall clearly warn the offending player that the mouthguard must be in the proper position while participating.

front: What is the penalty for a second or subsequent infraction of not wearing a mouthguard properly? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 3
back: Loss of 5 yards from the point where the ball would have been put into play. The player shall be removed until properly equipped, with immediate substitution allowed.

front: What are the specifications for acceptable cleated shoes? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 4
back: A minimum of 7 cleats per sole with a minimum cleat tip diameter of 3/16 inch (4.8 mm). Additional cleats may have a lesser tip diameter, provided the maximum length is 1/2 inch (12.7 mm). The maximum cleat length is 1/2 inch (12.7 mm).

front: What types of cleats are illegal? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 4
back: Cleats made of metal or with a metal tip, or made of any material that burrs, chips, or fractures, are illegal.

front: What is the penalty for illegal footwear? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 4
back: Loss of 5 yards from the point where the ball would have been put into play, or added to the penalty for any other foul. If more than 1 player offends on the same play, only 1 penalty L5 will be applied. The offending player is removed until illegal equipment is replaced, with immediate substitution and no game delay.

front: What must the head coach or designated representative certify to the umpire before the game? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 5
back: They must certify that all players have been informed of mandatory and illegal equipment, provided with mandatory equipment, instructed on how to wear it, and instructed to notify coaching staff if equipment becomes illegal during the game.

front: What are the specifications for the distance chain? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 6
back: Two rods connected by a chain exactly 10 yards (10 metres) long. Rods must be wood or aluminum, at least 6 feet (1.8 metres) high, preferably with a distinctive marking device at the top.

front: What are the specifications for the downsbox? Rule 1 | Section 11 | Article 6
back: A wooden or aluminum post with plates or a box numbered 1 to 3, with numbers at least 10 inches (25 cm) high and clearly visible to all officials and players.

front: What is the pre-game requirement for all players concerning registration? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 1
back: All players must be registered by name and number with the scorer prior to the start of the game.

front: What is the penalty if an offending player is not registered according to the rule? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 1
back: The offending player shall be removed from the game until the score sheet has been corrected. An immediate substitution will be made, but the game shall not be delayed.

front: Are scores made by a non-registered player considered legal? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 1 Note 1
back: Yes, any score made by a non-registered player is legal, provided the player is then registered on the score sheet.

front: When may substitutes enter the field of play? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 2a
back: Substitutes may enter the field of play only when the ball is dead.

front: Where must a player leaving the game proceed? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 2b
back: A player leaving the game shall proceed directly to the sideline on which their bench is located, and then to the team bench in the out-of-bounds area.

front: When do sideline officials stop observing for possible substitutes? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 2c
back: Sideline officials stop observing for possible substitutes and raise their arms to shoulder level as soon as Team A breaks its huddle.

front: What is considered illegal regarding the use of substitution proceedings to deceive an opponent? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 2d
back: The use of substitution proceedings, or alleged substitution proceedings, to deceive the opponent is illegal, specifically if a "sleeper play" occurs on the subsequent play after one or more Team A players or substitutes legally enter or leave the field.

front: How is a "sleeper play" defined? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 2d
back: A "sleeper play" is defined as a pass play or kick play designed to deceive the opponent, which occurs when an A player remains at the sideline adjacent to their team bench area, often with the ball on the opposite side of the field, and Team A lines up quickly, snaps the ball, and throws a forward pass or lateral to the remote A player.

front: What is the penalty for using substitution proceedings to deceive an opponent with a sleeper play for Team A? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 2d Penalty
back: Team A 1.2D –L10 DR, 3D DG –L10 DR, 3D DNG-LB, PBD.

front: Under what condition must a substitute who enters the field remain for the subsequent play? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 2e
back: A substitute who enters the field to the extent to be able to communicate with a teammate must remain on the field for the subsequent play.

front: What is the penalty for a substitute who enters the field, communicates, but does not remain for the subsequent play? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 2e Penalty
back: Team A 1.2D – L10 DR, 3D DG-L10 DR, 3D DNG-LB PBD. Team B L10.

front: What is the maximum number of players and/or substitutes a team is allowed to have on the field during a play? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 3
back: It is illegal for a team to have more than 12 players and/or substitutes on the field during a play.

front: What is the penalty for a team having more than 12 players and/or substitutes on the field during a play? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 3 Penalty
back: Team A 1.2D-L10 DR, 3D DG-L10 DR, 3D DNG-LB PBD. Team B L10.

front: Who is responsible for fielding the correct number of players? Rule 1 | Section 12 | Article 3 Note
back: Coaches, not officials, are responsible for fielding the correct number of players.

front: Who are the only people legally allowed on the sidelines during a game? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 1
back: During the game, the only persons who may legally occupy any position on the sidelines are: the field officials, the Downbox Official, the Yardstick Officials, the Time Keeper, and the Scorer.

front: Who is allowed in the team bench area during a game? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 1
back: During the game, the team bench area may be occupied only by substitute players, and other authorized non-playing personnel of the team, consisting of coaches, doctors, trainers, and equipment personnel.

front: What are the dimensions for the team bench area's location and enclosure? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 1
back: The team bench area shall be located a minimum of 5 yards (5 metres) and a maximum of 10 yards (10 metres) from the sideline. The area shall be enclosed by a line 4 inches (10 cm) wide, which is located at least 2 yards (2 metres) minimum, and 5 yards (5 metres) optimum from the sideline, and a line at each end of the bench 5 yards (5 metres) from the end.

front: What is the penalty for occupants of the team bench encroaching on the sidelines or playing field? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 1
back: Penalty: L10, no option, from point where the ball would have been put in play if no foul had occurred.

front: When is a conference between coaches and players at the sideline legal? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 2
back: During an official time out, a conference at the sideline between coaches and players of each team is legal. A similar conference is legal whenever the clock is stopped and a significant time delay occurs, e.g. a measurement, injury, TV commercial, etc.

front: What is the penalty if an unauthorized person acting to the advantage of the team in possession interferes with play, and a score would have been made? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 3
back: If it is obvious to the Referee that a score (such as a rouge or safety touch) would have been made, then the score will be awarded.

front: What is the penalty if an unauthorized person acting to the advantage of the team in possession interferes with play, and a score would NOT have been made? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 3
back: If it is not obvious that a score would have been made, the penalty is L10 PBH (Loss of 10 yards from the Point Behind the Ball).

front: What is the penalty if an unauthorized person acting to the advantage of the team not in possession interferes with play and it's obvious a touchdown would have been scored, or if the unauthorized person is a substitute, coach, trainer or other occupant of the team bench? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 3
back: A touchdown shall be awarded.

front: What is the penalty if an unauthorized person (not a substitute, coach, trainer, or other occupant of the team bench) interferes with a forward pass in the Field of Play, acting to the advantage of the team not in possession? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 3
back: Half the distance to the goal line from PF (Point of Foul).

front: What is the penalty if an unauthorized person (not a substitute, coach, trainer, or other occupant of the team bench) interferes with a forward pass in the End zone against Team A, acting to the advantage of the team not in possession? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 3
back: Award the ball to Team A at the 1 yard (1 metre) line (unless a touchdown is awarded).

front: What is the penalty if an unauthorized person touches or kicks a loose ball and it is obvious a score would have been made? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 3
back: The score will be awarded.

front: What is the penalty if an unauthorized person who is a substitute, coach, trainer, or other occupant of the team bench touches or kicks a loose ball? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 3
back: The team will be penalized half the distance to their goal line from PF (Point of Foul).

front: What is the penalty if an unauthorized person who is a substitute, coach, trainer, or other occupant of a team bench interferes with a player or a loose ball? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 3
back: Disqualification from further participation in any capacity.

front: Under what conditions can personnel enter the field during a stoppage in play? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 5
back: During a stoppage in play for injury, or other reason, personnel of each team shall be allowed to enter the field with the Referee’s permission.

front: What activities are personnel allowed to undertake when entering the field during a stoppage for injury or other reasons? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 5
back: Such personnel may attend to the injured player or bring water to the players on the field, but shall not undertake any coaching activities.

front: If a player leaves the game due to an injury, for how many plays are they required to be off the field? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 5
back: When play has been stopped for a player injury, that player shall be required to leave the game for at least three plays.

front: If a player leaves the game due to equipment repair, for how many plays are they required to be off the field? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 5
back: When play has been stopped for equipment repair, that player shall be required to leave the game for at least one play.

front: What is the penalty if a player who was required to leave the game for injury or equipment repair does not do so? Rule 1 | Section 13 | Article 5
back: L10, no option.

front: What is the subject of Rule 2? Rule 2 | Officials
back: Officials

front: What are the designated roles of field officials for a 7-official crew? Rule 2 | Section 1 | Article 1
back: Referee (R), Umpire (U), Field Judge (FJ), Back Umpire (BU), Back Judge (BJ), Down Judge (DJ), Line Judge (LJ), and Side Judge (SJ).

front: What are the designated roles of field officials for a 5-official crew? Rule 2 | Section 1 | Article 1
back: Referee (R), Umpire (U), Back Judge (BJ), Down Judge (DJ), Line Judge (LJ), and Side Judge (SJ).

front: What are the designated roles of field officials for a 3-official crew? Rule 2 | Section 1 | Article 1
back: Referee (R), Umpire (U), Line Judge (LJ), and Side Judge (SJ).

front: How many officials may be designated per game, as specified by the governing authority? Rule 2 | Section 1 | Article 1
back: The number of officials per game may be from 1 to 7.

front: Who are the designated sideline officials? Rule 2 | Section 1 | Article 2
back: Downbox Official, Yardstick Official (2 or 3), Timekeeper, and Scorer.

front: How is the number of officials per game determined? Rule 2 | Section 1 | Article 3
back: The number of officials per game shall be in accordance with the recommendations of the local, provincial, or national officials’ associations.

front: Where are the responsibilities, positioning, and mechanics of officials covered? Rule 2 | Section 1 | Article 3
back: Responsibilities, positioning, and mechanics are covered in the CFOA/Football Canada Officials’ Training Manual.

front: What is the primary responsibility of all field officials in a game? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: All field officials are equally responsible for the orderly conduct of the game and the enforcement of the rules.

front: What action must field officials take if they recognize a player showing signs consistent with a concussion? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: All field officials, upon recognizing any player who shows signs, symptoms, or behaviors consistent with a concussion, shall report their concerns through the Referee to the head coach or appropriate health-care professional.

front: What equipment must each field official have? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 2
back: Each field official shall be equipped with a whistle and a "red" coloured marker.

front: What is the effect of sounding a whistle when the ball is in play? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: The sounding of a whistle when the ball is in play shall cause the ball to be ruled dead, and shall stop the game.

front: When should the whistle NOT be sounded in the event of an injury? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: The whistle should not be sounded in the event of injury until the ball is dead.

front: What signal indicates an infraction, and when does play stop after this signal? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: The throwing of the marker shall indicate an infraction, but play shall continue until the sounding of a whistle.

front: What signal does the Referee use to indicate that the ball is ready for play and that "time is in"? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 5
back: The Referee shall sound the whistle to indicate that the ball is ready for play, and shall signal that "time is in" by a downward sweep of the arm from the overhead position.

front: Who should mark the out-of-bounds spot when the ball goes out of bounds? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 6
back: The nearest official should mark the out-of-bounds spot when the ball goes out of bounds.

front: When a foul is called, when should the official report it to the Referee? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 8
back: When a foul is called, the official shall report it to the Referee immediately if the ball is dead, or if the ball is alive, as soon as it is dead.

front: What actions will the Referee take after a foul has been reported to them? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 9
back: When a foul has been reported to the Referee, the Referee will indicate the number of the player who committed the foul, give the penalty signal, assess the penalty, and signal that the ball is again ready for play.

front: What is the official's responsibility regarding forward progress once the ball has been whistled dead? Rule 2 | Section 2 | Article 10
back: When the ball has been whistled dead, the appropriate official shall mark the spot of forward progress of the ball, which will be the point of the subsequent play.

front: What is the Referee's primary responsibility during a game? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 1
back: The Referee shall take primary charge of the game, and shall guide and direct the work of the other officials.

front: When can the Referee overrule another official's decision? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 1
back: The Referee may overrule any other official.

front: What is the Referee's role concerning game balls before the game? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 1
back: The Referee shall test the game balls 30 minutes before the game, and the Referee’s decision shall be final as to the suitability of the balls.

front: What action must the Referee take regarding field markings or ground rules before a game? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 2
back: The Referee shall report any irregularities in field markings, or ground rules, to the captains before the game, and review these with the other officials before the game.

front: What must the Referee explain to the non-offending captain when a foul is called? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 3
back: When a foul is called, the Referee shall explain to the non-offending captain the application of the penalty, or any option to which the captain is entitled if they refuse the penalty.

front: Who is responsible for keeping count of the downs? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 4
back: The Referee shall keep count of the downs, subject to a check with the Down Judge.

front: Who serves as the sole communication link between officials and team captains or coaches? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 5
back: The Referee shall be the sole means of communication between the officials and the team captains or coaches.

front: How are 3-minute warnings in each half communicated? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 6
back: The Referee shall be notified by the Down Judge or Line Judge, when 3 minutes of play remains in each half. The Referee shall notify the captains, and the nearest official shall notify the coaches of each team.

front: How does the Referee indicate the end of playing time in each period? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 7
back: The Referee shall indicate that playing time has ended in each period, by sounding the whistle and signaling to the Timer.

front: What action does the Referee take regarding the half time interval? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 8
back: The Referee shall have the captains of each team warned when 3 minutes remains in the half time interval.

front: What is the Referee's primary responsibility regarding Team A's actions? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 9
back: The Referee shall take primary charge of Team A, and shall take a position behind Team A. The Referee is responsible to determine if the ball is put into play legally, cover the action of the passer and the kicker and their opponents.

front: Who is responsible for marking the out-of-bounds spot when a ball goes out of bounds in flight? Rule 2 | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 9
back: The Referee shall be responsible for marking the out-of-bounds spot when a ball goes out of bounds in flight.

front: What is the primary jurisdiction of the Umpire? Rule 2 | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 1
back: The Umpire shall have primary jurisdiction over the actions of players of both teams on the line of scrimmage.

front: Where does the Umpire position themselves? Rule 2 | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 1
back: The Umpire shall take a position behind the defensive line of Team B.

front: What are the Umpire's responsibilities regarding linebackers? Rule 2 | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 2
back: The Umpire shall supervise the linebackers and their use of hands on eligible pass receivers of Team A.

front: What types of passes and kicks does the Umpire cover? Rule 2 | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 2
back: The Umpire shall cover short forward passes and short kicks over the centre of the line.

front: What is the Umpire's role regarding Team A's ineligible receivers on the line of scrimmage? Rule 2 | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 2
back: The Umpire shall check that Team A ineligible receivers on the line of scrimmage do not proceed downfield before a forward pass is thrown.

front: How does the Umpire assist with crack-back blocking? Rule 2 | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 2
back: The Umpire shall assist in coverage of crack-back blocking in the restricted area.

front: What is the primary jurisdictional area of the Back Umpire? Rule 2 | Section 5 – Back Umpire (BU) | Article 1
back: The Back Umpire has primary jurisdiction over the actions of players of both teams behind the Team B line.

front: Where should the Back Umpire position themselves according to Article 1? Rule 2 | Section 5 – Back Umpire (BU) | Article 1
back: The Back Umpire should take a position behind the deepest Team B player.

front: What type of passes and kicks is the Back Umpire responsible for covering? Rule 2 | Section 5 – Back Umpire (BU) | Article 2
back: The Back Umpire shall cover long passes in the centre of the field and kicks downfield.

front: Under what condition does the Back Umpire rule on field goal attempts? Rule 2 | Section 5 – Back Umpire (BU) | Article 2
back: The Back Umpire shall rule field goal attempts successful or not, specifically from outside the 10 yard (metre) line.

front: What are the duties of the Back Judge? Rule 2 | Section 6: Back Judge (BJ)
back: The duties of the Back Judge shall be identical with those of the Back Umpire.

front: What are the Down Judge's primary responsibilities regarding the line of scrimmage and neutral zone? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 1
back: The Down Judge shall be responsible for the general supervision of the line of scrimmage, the neutral zone, and the actions of the end and flankers on his/her side of the field.

front: Where does the Down Judge position themselves at the start of a play? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 1
back: The Down Judge shall take up a position on the line of scrimmage at a suitable distance in from the sideline on the same side of the field as the distance chain and Downsbox.

front: What specific type of blocking is the Down Judge primarily responsible for covering at the snap? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 1
back: The Down Judge shall be primarily responsible to cover crack-back blocking by players positioned on their side of the field when the ball is snapped.

front: What actions related to passes and kicks is the Down Judge responsible for, when appropriate? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 2
back: The Down Judge shall, when appropriate: a) Cover passes down his/her side of the field. b) Cover kicks down his/her side of the field.

front: What are the Down Judge's responsibilities regarding substitutions? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 3
back: The Down Judge shall: a) Systematically check his/her sideline for substitutes, and ensure legality of substitution procedures.

front: When does the Down Judge notify the Referee about remaining time in each half and period? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 3
back: The Down Judge shall: b) Notify the Referee when 3 minutes remain in each half, after being so notified by the timekeeper. c) Notify the Referee when 1 minute remains in each period, after being so notified by the timekeeper.

front: Who supervises the placement of the distance chain and Downsbox, and under whose direction? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 4
back: The Down Judge shall: a) Supervise the Yardstick officials and the Dowbox official in the placement of the distance chain and Downsbox, under the direction of the Referee.

front: What is the Down Judge's role in keeping track of downs? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 4
back: The Down Judge shall: b) Keep an accurate count of the downs to assist the Referee.

front: What is the Down Judge's responsibility for the distance chain at the end of the 1st and 3rd periods? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 4
back: The Down Judge shall: c) Be responsible for changing the position of the distance chain at the end of the 1st and 3rd periods to the identical spot, at the opposite end of the field, corresponding to the point at which play ended in that period.

front: During a measurement, what is the Down Judge's specific task related to the distance chain? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 4
back: The Down Judge shall: d) When a measure is required by the Referee, mark on the chain the spot corresponding to the far side of the cross stripe which is farthest from the ball within the span of the distance chain, and have the Yardstick Official bring the distance chain to the Referee.

front: What must the Down Judge do regarding penalties and distances? Rule 2 | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 4
back: The Down Judge shall: e) Check distance applied on penalties.

front: What are the responsibilities of the Line Judge? Rule 2 | Section 8: Line Judge (LJ) | Article 1
back: The duties of the Line Judge shall be identical to those of the Down Judge covered in Section 7, Articles 1 to 3 inclusive, only.

front: Where is the Side Judge typically positioned on the field? Rule 2 | Section 9: Side Judge (SJ) | Article 1
back: On or near the sideline approximately eighteen to twenty yards in advance of the line of scrimmage.

front: Which official does the Side Judge work the same side of the field as? Rule 2 | Section 9: Side Judge (SJ) | Article 1
back: The Down Judge.

front: Under whose direction do the Downbox and Yardstick Officials act? Rule 2 | Section 10: Downbox and Yardstick Officials | Article 1
back: They shall act under the direction of the Down Judge.

front: Where must the Downsbox and distance chain be positioned? Rule 2 | Section 10: Downbox and Yardstick Officials | Article 1
back: The Downsbox and distance chain shall be positioned out of bounds.

front: What is the responsibility of the Downbox Official regarding the Downsbox? Rule 2 | Section 10: Downbox and Yardstick Officials | Article 2
back: The Downbox Official shall place the Downsbox at the point where the ball is to be scrimmaged, and indicate the number of each down on the Downsbox.

front: Who directs the placement of the distance chain by the Yardstick Officials? Rule 2 | Section 10: Downbox and Yardstick Officials | Article 3
back: The two Yardstick Officials shall place the distance chain as directed by the Down Judge.

front: When a 3rd Yardstick Official is used, what is the purpose of their marker rod? Rule 2 | Section 10: Downbox and Yardstick Officials | Article 4
back: If a 3rd Yardstick Official is used to hold a single marker rod on the sideline opposite the 10 yard (10 metre) objective line, this marker will not be used to determine whether a first down has been gained.

front: Under whose direction may penalties be recorded by a 3rd Yardstick Official? Rule 2 | Section 10: Downbox and Yardstick Officials | Article 4
back: Under the direction of the Referee, penalties may be recorded by a 3rd Yardstick Official.

front: What information must the Scorer be provided with prior to the game? Rule 2 | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 1
back: The Scorer shall be provided with a complete list of the eligible competing players, including names and correct numbers.

front: Who must the scoresheet be presented to for signature after the game? Rule 2 | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 1
back: The scoresheet must be presented to the Referee after the game for signature.

front: How many timing devices should be used if two timekeepers are appointed? Rule 2 | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 2
back: If 2 timekeepers are appointed, they shall use one timing device.

front: Who operates the timing device when two timekeepers are appointed? Rule 2 | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 2
back: When two timekeepers are appointed, one of them shall operate the timing device solely.

front: Who settles disagreements between timekeepers? Rule 2 | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 2
back: In the event of disagreement between timekeepers, the Referee shall be called immediately to settle any dispute or make any necessary adjustment.

front: When does the Timekeeper notify the Down Judge or Line Judge about remaining time? Rule 2 | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 3
back: The Timekeeper shall notify the Down Judge or the Line Judge when 3 minutes remain in the 2nd and 4th periods, and when 1 minute remains in each period.

front: What action does the Timekeeper take at the commencement of the last minute of play in each period? Rule 2 | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 4
back: At the commencement of the last minute of play, the Timekeeper will raise the flag and continue to keep it raised until the watch registers full time for the period.

front: What happens if the ball becomes dead during the last minute of play and the Timekeeper's flag is still raised? Rule 2 | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 4
back: If the ball becomes dead on any play and the flag is still raised, the ball will again be put into play.

front: Under what condition is a period declared over by the Referee during the last minute of play? Rule 2 | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 4
back: If the flag has been lowered since the last time the ball was put into play, the period will be over, and so declared by the Referee, subject to fouls committed during the last play.

front: How many points are awarded for a Touchdown? Rule 3 | Scoring | Table of Scores
back: 6 Points

front: What is the point value of a Rouge? Rule 3 | Scoring | Table of Scores
back: 1 Point

front: How many points does a Field Goal award? Rule 3 | Scoring | Table of Scores
back: 3 Points

front: What are the possible point values for a Convert? Rule 3 | Scoring | Table of Scores
back: 1 or 2 Points

front: How many points is a Safety Touch worth? Rule 3 | Scoring | Table of Scores
back: 2 Points

front: Which team is declared the winner? Rule 3 | Scoring | Table of Scores
back: The team scoring the majority of the points.

front: Under what conditions is a touchdown scored when the ball is in the opponent's end zone? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Touchdown
back: A touchdown is scored when the ball is in the opponent’s end zone in possession of a player, or when a forward pass is legally completed in the opponent’s end zone.

front: When is a touchdown scored in relation to the goal line? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Touchdown
back: A touchdown is scored when the ball in the possession of a player crosses or touches the goal line, or the plane of the goal line, even in the air.

front: What are the options for the team scored against after a touchdown? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Touchdown
back: After a touchdown, the team scored against may elect to have the play put into play by kicking off from its own 45 yard (40 metre) line or by requiring the scoring team to kick off from its 45 yard (40 metre) line.

front: How is a field goal scored by a drop or place kick? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Field Goal
back: A field goal is scored by a drop or place kick (except on a kick off) when the ball, after being kicked and without again touching the ground, goes over the crossbar and between the goal posts (or goal posts produced) of the opponent’s goal, regardless of whether it touches the goal post assembly.

front: What happens if the ball touches a player after being kicked but still goes over the crossbar and between the goal posts? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Field Goal
back: If, after being kicked, the ball touches, or is touched by any player before it crosses the line of scrimmage; or touches or is touched by a B player after it crosses the line of scrimmage; and the ball continues forward in the air over the cross bar between the goal posts, the field goal shall score.

front: What are the options for the team scored against after a field goal? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Field Goal
back: After a field goal, the team scored against may elect to have the ball put into play by scrimmaging the ball at its own 35 yard (30 Metre) line, by kicking off from its own 35 yard (30 metre) line, or by requiring the scoring team to kick off from its 45 yard (40 metre) line.

front: When is a safety touch scored? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Safety Touch
back: A safety touch is scored when the ball becomes dead in possession of a team in its own end zone, or goes out of bounds in the end zone, as a result of the ball having been carried, kicked, fumbled or otherwise directed from the field of play into the end zone by the team scored against, or as a DIRECT result of a kick being blocked in the field of play.

front: What happens if a player intercepts a forward pass in the field of play and their momentum carries them into their own end zone? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Safety Touch
back: If a player intercepts a forward pass in the field of play while moving toward the player’s goal line, and in the judgment of the official, the momentum carries the player into the player’s end zone, possession is deemed to have been gained in the end zone, resulting in a safety touch.

front: What is the consequence for the scoring team after a safety touch? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Safety Touch
back: After a safety touch, the scoring team will scrimmage the ball from its own 35-yard (30 metre) line.

front: When is a rouge (single point) scored? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Rouge or Single Point
back: A rouge is scored when the ball becomes dead in possession of a team in its own end zone, or goes out of bounds in its end zone, as a result of the ball having been kicked into the end zone by an opponent.

front: Under what condition is possession deemed to have been gained in the end zone for a kicked ball leading to a rouge? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Rouge or Single Point
back: If a player catches a kicked ball in the field of play while moving toward their goal line, and in the judgment of the official, this momentum carries them into their team’s end zone, possession is deemed to have been gained in the end zone.

front: What happens if a kick-off is kicked directly out of bounds in flight in the end zone? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Rouge or Single Point
back: If a kick-off is kicked directly out of bounds, in flight in the end zone, no point will be awarded, and the ball will be scrimmaged by the receiving team – 1D at their own 20 yard (20 metre) line, at any point on or between the hash marks.

front: What are the options for the team scored against after a rouge resulting from an unsuccessful field goal attempt? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Rouge or Single Point
back: If a rouge was scored as a result of an unsuccessful field goal attempt, the team scored against may choose to scrimmage at any point on or between the hash marks on their own 35 yard (30 metre) line, or at any point on or between the hash marks at the previous line of scrimmage.

front: How many points are awarded for a field goal attempt on a convert? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Convert
back: One (1) point is awarded for kicking a field goal on a convert attempt.

front: How many points are awarded for scoring a touchdown on a convert attempt? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Convert
back: Two (2) points are awarded for scoring a touchdown on a convert attempt.

front: What types of kicks are prohibited during a convert attempt? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Convert
back: A punt or onside kick is prohibited during a convert attempt.

front: What is the penalty for an illegal interference on a forward pass by Team B during a convert attempt? Rule 3 | Section 2 – Definitions | Article: Convert
back: For an illegal interference on a forward pass by Team B, Team A shall repeat the convert attempt at the Team B 1 yard (1 metre) line, or 15 yards in advance of the PLS whichever is closer to Team A goal line, or repeat the convert at the PLS and apply the penalty (L15) on the kick off.

front: What defines the line of scrimmage? Rule 4 | Section: SCRIMMAGE | Article 1
back:
The line of scrimmage is an imaginary line, extending from sideline to sideline, parallel to the goal line and passing through the point of the ball farthest from Team A


s goal line.

front: What are the dimensions of the neutral zone? Rule 4 | Section: SCRIMMAGE | Article 2
back: The neutral zone is the area from the line of scrimmage to 1 yard (1 metre) in advance of the line of scrimmage, extending from sideline to sideline.

front: How is the close line play area defined? Rule 4 | Section: SCRIMMAGE | Article 3
back:
The close line play area is defined as the area bounded by the outer shoulder of the offensive tight ends or positions ordinarily occupied by the tight end, within 2 yards either side of the line of scrimmage (Total 4 yards 


4 metres).

front: What criteria define line players of Team A? Rule 4 | Section: SCRIMMAGE | Article 4
back: Line players of team A are those players whose head and shoulders are within 1 yard (1 metre) and on their own side of the line of scrimmage and are formed in a single line when the ball is snapped.

front: Who are considered eligible receivers among Team A line players? Rule 4 | Section: SCRIMMAGE | Article 4
back: Line players include the 5 ineligible receivers and the two eligible receivers, one at each end.

front: Under what conditions can a Team A player in the backfield be considered an eligible receiver? Rule 4 | Section: SCRIMMAGE | Article 4
back: Any Team A player(s) in the backfield, while moving forward, anywhere between the eligible end(s) and tackle(s), shall also be considered eligible receiver(s) as long as they remain onside at the time the ball is snapped. This will include the player occupying the position of quarterback.

front: What is the penalty for a Team A player being in a doubtful position regarding the line of scrimmage at the snap? Rule 4 | Section: SCRIMMAGE | Article 4
back:
Penalty: 1.2D 


L5 DR; 3D DG 


L5 DR; DNG 


LB PBD.

front: When a Rule 4 violation occurs before the snap, what action can officials take? Rule 4 | Section: SCRIMMAGE | Article 5
back: Where a violation under Rule 4 occurs prior to the snap of the ball, the officials are empowered to stop the play immediately.

front: What happens to the down if a Rule 4 pre-snap violation occurs and the penalty distance is declined? Rule 4 | Section: SCRIMMAGE | Article 5
back: The down will be repeated, without option, at the appropriate point, after the acceptance or declination of the penalty distance.

front: What defines the blocking below the waist zone? Rule 4 | Section: SCRIMMAGE | Article 6
back: The blocking below the waist zone is defined as an area bounded by the outer shoulder of the offensive tight ends or the positions ordinarily occupied by the tight end, within 2 yards of the defensive side of the line of scrimmage extending back to the initial position of the quarterback, running back (in normal position) or kicker.

front: What is the primary action a Team A centre must perform to put the ball in play on a scrimmage play? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The centre of Team A shall put the ball in play by "snapping" it between the legs in one continuous motion in the direction from toe to heel.

front: After the ball is snapped, when can the centre handle the ball again? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The ball must leave the center’s hand or hands and the centre shall not handle it again until it has been in possession of another player.

front: Under what conditions can a player who is not officially the centre be considered the centre for the purpose of snapping the ball? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: Any player who takes a position over the ball, with one or both hands on the ball, shall snap the ball, and be considered as the centre.

front: What is the penalty for a centre intentionally moving the ball as if to snap it to draw opponents offside? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The penalty is 1.2D-L5 DR, 3D DG-L5 DR, 3D DNG-LB PBD.

front: What types of actions by either team are considered misleading tactics designed to draw an opponent offside? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 2
back: No player of either team shall make a motion obviously designed to draw an opponent offside. No player of either team shall voice a signal which, in the opinion of the official, draws an opponent offside.

front: When can a Team A quarterback be penalized for misleading tactics related to the snap? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 2
back: Team A shall be penalized if the quarterback: a) makes a quick movement towards the centre, without the ball being immediately snapped, or b) assumes a stance with his/her hands under the centre, and makes such motion as bobbing head, moving shoulders, or flexing knees in a jerky motion without the ball being snapped, or c) assumes a stance with his/her hands under the centre and moves away quickly from the centre without the ball being snapped.

front: What is the penalty for Team A committing misleading tactics? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 2
back: The penalty for Team A is 1.2D – L5 DR, 3D DG-L5 DR, 3D DNG – LB PBD.

front: Under what condition is a player allowed to be in the neutral zone before the ball is snapped? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: The head, arms and hands of the centre may be in advance of the line of scrimmage.

front: What happens if a Team B player goes offside and breaks the plane of the line of scrimmage before the snap? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: The officials shall stop the play immediately, and award the penalty, subject to the right of Team A to decline the penalty and have the same down repeated as though a foul had not occurred.

front: What is the penalty for offside by Team A or Team B? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: The penalty for Team A is 1.2D – L5 DR, 3D DG – L5 DR, 3D DNG – LB PBD. The penalty for Team B is L5.

front: How much time does the Referee allow for the ball to be put into play? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: The Referee shall allow 20 seconds for the ball to be put into play.

front: When is Team A given a full 20 seconds to snap the ball after the game is stopped during the time count? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: Team A will receive a full 20 seconds to snap the ball if the game is stopped due to: a time out request by either team, a foul by either team, or a reason associated with Team B (substitution of 3 or more players, player injury, player equipment, etc.).

front: What is the penalty for a time count violation before the 3-minute warning signal and in overtime? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: The penalty is 1, 2, 3D – L5 DR.

front: What is the penalty for a time count violation after the 3-minute warning signal in any half? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: For 1st or 2nd down, it is Team B option LD or L10DR. For 3rd down, it is L10DR.

front: What happens if Team A has two consecutive time count penalties? Rule 4 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: The Referee will order Team A to put the ball in play legally within 20 seconds or forfeit possession to Team B.

front: What are the legal numbers for players in Canadian football? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: Legal numbers are from 0 to 99 inclusive.

front: What numbering system identifies eligible pass receivers for Team A? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: Eligible Pass Receivers are identified by numbers 0 to 49, and 80 to 99.

front: What numbering system identifies ineligible pass receivers for Team A? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: Ineligible Pass Receivers are identified by numbers 50 to 79.

front: Under what condition can an inappropriately numbered player be an eligible or ineligible receiver? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: On any given play from scrimmage, any number of positions may be occupied by inappropriately numbered players who have reported to the Referee as eligible or ineligible receivers.

front: How many Team A players must be within 1 yard and on their own side of the line of scrimmage when the ball is put into play, excluding the quarterback? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 2
