back: At least seven Team A players must be within 1 yard (1 metre) and on their own side of the line of scrimmage, not including the player in the position usually occupied by the quarterback.

front: When can a player at either end of the line of scrimmage be in motion? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: The player who, at the snap of the ball is occupying a position at either end of the line of scrimmage may be in motion while within 1 yard of the line of scrimmage but must not be moving towards the opponent’s goal line when the ball is put into play.

front: What happens if Team A has fewer than 7 players on the line due to a Team A offside? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: If Team A has fewer than 7 players on the line due to a Team A offside, the penalty shall be for offside only.

front: How many interior line players must Team A have, identified as ineligible pass receivers, and how must they be positioned? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: Team A shall have at least 5 interior line players identified as ineligible pass receivers, who must be positioned in a continuous, unbroken line.

front: In addition to interior line players, how many players at each end of the line must be identified as eligible receivers? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: One player at each end of the line shall be identified as an eligible receiver.

front: What motion is prohibited for Team A Line Players after assuming a three-point or four-point stance? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: Team A Line Players after having assumed a three-point or four-point stance may not break their stance by lifting a hand.

front: What must all Team A Line Players, including the Centre, do immediately prior to the snap of the ball? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: All Team A Line Players, including the Centre, must become stationary and remain motionless for at least one second immediately prior to the snap of the ball.

front: What motion is the centre allowed to make prior to the snap? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: The centre is allowed to make the motion which is necessary to snap the ball, but may not break their 3- or 4-point stance on the ball, to allow another player to become the centre.

front: What is the penalty for a violation of the stance and motion rules for Team A Line Players? Rule 4 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: The penalty is: 1.2D – L5 DR, 3D DG – L5 DR, 3D DNG – LB PBD.

front: When can Team A choose the ball's placement on or between the hash marks after certain plays or fouls? Rule 4 | Section 4: Points of Scrimmage Restrictions | Article 1
back: Team A may elect to put the ball into play at any point on or between the hash marks after a scoring play, after the ball has been declared dead in the end zone, following a penalty for a foul in the end zone or on a convert, or if the ball strikes the goal post assembly in flight, unless a rule specifies the PLS as the next point of scrimmage.

front: What happens if a rule specifies the PLS as the next point of scrimmage, even after an event where Team A might normally choose ball placement? Rule 4 | Section 4: Points of Scrimmage Restrictions | Article 1
back: If a rule specifies that the next point of scrimmage is the PLS, the ball will be placed at that specific spot.

front: Where is the ball scrimmaged if it becomes dead within 24 yards (22 metres) of the sideline or goes out of bounds? Rule 4 | Section 4: Points of Scrimmage Restrictions | Article 2
back: It shall next be scrimmaged 24 yards (22 metres) in from that sideline at the yardage point where it became dead.

front: What is the point of scrimmage if Team A has possession of the ball within 1 yard (1 metre) of either goal line? Rule 4 | Section 4: Points of Scrimmage Restrictions | Article 3
back: It shall be scrimmaged on the 1 yard (1 metre) line.

front: Under what specific conditions on 3rd down can Team A position the ball away from the goal posts due to wet ground? Rule 4 | Section 4: Points of Scrimmage Restrictions | Article 4
back: In the case of wet ground, on 3rd down on or within their own 15 yard (15 metre) line, Team A may position the ball away from the goal posts at the closest hash mark, or closest suitable spot to that point.

front: When can Team A position the ball away from the goal posts at the closest hash mark or suitable spot on any down due to wet ground? Rule 4 | Section 4: Points of Scrimmage Restrictions | Article 5
back: In the case of wet ground, on any down on or within their own 5 yard (5 metre) line, Team A may position the ball away from the goal posts at the closest hash mark, or closest suitable spot to that point.

front: What is the definition of interference in the context of this rulebook? Rule 4 | SECTION 5: INTERFERENCE | Article 1
back: Interference is a general term, applicable to both teams, committed when a player obstructs, blocks, or charges against an opponent, even without direct contact, preventing their approach to the ball carrier, potential ball carrier, or the ball.

front: How is 'screening' defined in relation to interference? Rule 4 | SECTION 5: INTERFERENCE | Article 1
back: Screening is interference without direct contact.

front: What constitutes 'blocking below the waist'? Rule 4 | SECTION 5: INTERFERENCE | Article 1
back: Blocking below the waist is making initial contact below the waist against an opponent, other than the ball carrier, with any part of the blocker's body.

front: Under what conditions is the use of hands and arms in blocking considered legal? Rule 4 | SECTION 5: INTERFERENCE | Article 1
back: The use of hands and arms is legal if: hands are slightly behind, even with, or in advance of elbows; arms are fully extended; hands are open (palms facing opponent) or cupped/closed (palms not facing opponent); hands and arms are not used to strike, punch, grasp, pull, encircle, lift, hook, lock, or clamp; and hands are not clasped or locked. On a rolling or cross body block, hands may also be legally extended from the body.

front: When may Team A players interfere with opponents on a play from scrimmage? Rule 4 | SECTION 5: INTERFERENCE | Article 2
back: On any play from scrimmage, except when the ball is kicked across the line of scrimmage, all Team A players may interfere with opponents from deadline to deadline.

front: When is it illegal for a Team A player to block an opponent below the waist on a play from scrimmage? Rule 4 | SECTION 5: INTERFERENCE | Article 2
back: On any play from scrimmage, it is illegal for a player to block an opponent below the waist except as per Rule 7 Section 3 Article 19.

front: On a play from scrimmage, how may Team B players use their hands and arms against Team A? Rule 4 | SECTION 5: INTERFERENCE | Article 3
back: On any play from scrimmage, B players may use their hands and arms to reach the ball carrier, but shall not hold or encircle any A player other than the ball carrier.

front: When is it illegal for a Team B player to block an opponent below the waist on a play from scrimmage? Rule 4 | SECTION 5: INTERFERENCE | Article 3
back: On any play from scrimmage, it is illegal for a player to block an opponent below the waist except as per Rule 7 Section 3 Article 19.

front: How many attempts (downs) does the team in possession have to gain 10 yards (10 metres) after a kick-off? Rule 4 | Section 6: Miscellaneous | Article 1
back: The team in possession shall have 3 attempts (downs) to gain the required distance of 10 yards (10 metres).

front: What are the ways a team may advance the ball during a down? Rule 4 | Section 6: Miscellaneous | Article 1
back: It may be advanced by carrying it, kicking it, or throwing it.

front: What happens if Team A does not gain the required 10 yards in a series of downs? Rule 4 | Section 6: Miscellaneous | Article 1
back: The ball shall be awarded to the opponents as 1st down at the point where the ball becomes dead.

front: When measuring for a 1st down, which part of the ball is the determining point? Rule 4 | Section 6: Miscellaneous | Article 2
back: The forward point of the ball, not its centre, shall be the determining point.

front: Can a touchdown be awarded as a result of rotating the ball for measurement? Rule 4 | Section 6: Miscellaneous | Article 2
back: No, a touchdown cannot be awarded as a result of this rotation.

front: What is the penalty for a Team A teammate helping the ball carrier by grasping, pulling, pushing, or charging into him/her to assist forward progress on 1st or 2nd down? Rule 4 | Section 6: Miscellaneous | Article 3
back: Team A – 1,2D –L5 DR.

front: What is the penalty for a Team A teammate helping the ball carrier by grasping, pulling, pushing, or charging into him/her to assist forward progress on 3rd down when the distance is gained (DG)? Rule 4 | Section 6: Miscellaneous | Article 3
back: Team A – 3D DG –L5 PBH.

front: What is the penalty for Team A players holding hands or locking arms in making a block on 1st or 2nd down? Rule 4 | Section 6: Miscellaneous | Article 4
back: Team A – 1.2D – L10 DR.

front: What is the penalty for Team B players holding hands or locking arms in an effort to break up interference protecting the ball carrier? Rule 4 | Section 6: Miscellaneous | Article 4
back: Team B – L10 PLS or PBH.

front: What is the penalty for Team A players holding hands or locking arms in making a block? Rule 5 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: The penalty for Team A is 1st or 2nd Down Loss of 10 yards, Down Repeated (1.2D L10 DR); 3rd Down Gain, Loss of 10 yards, Down Repeated (3D DG L10 DR); or 3rd Down No Gain, Loss of Ball, Play Blown Dead (3D DNG LB PBD).

front: What is the penalty for Team B players holding hands or locking arms in an effort to break up interference protecting the ball carrier? Rule 5 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: The penalty for Team B is Loss of 10 yards from the Point of Last Scrimmage (PLS) or Point of Ball Held (PBH).

front: Under what condition is a ball ruled a fumble instead of a kick if it accidentally strikes a player's foot or leg? Rule 5 | Section 1 | Definitions | a)
back: If the ball accidentally strikes a player’s foot or leg while they are attempting to gain possession, it shall be ruled as a fumble if, in the official’s judgment, the player made no effort to kick the ball.

front: When making a place kick, what is the maximum height the lowest point of the ball can be above the ground if a tee is used? Rule 5 | Section 1 | Definitions | c)
back: The lowest point of the ball may not be more than 1 inch (2.54 cm) above the ground when a tee is used for a place kick.

front: Under what conditions does an offside player become an onside player after the ball has been kicked towards the opponent's deadline? Rule 5 | Section 1 | Definitions | j)
back: An offside player becomes an onside player when the ball, after being kicked towards the opponent’s deadline, touches an opponent, the kicker, or another onside player.

front: What is the exception to an offside player becoming onside if a Team B player touches the ball on a kick from scrimmage? Rule 5 | Section 1 | Definitions | j)
back: If on a kick from scrimmage a Team B player touches the ball before it crosses the line of scrimmage, such touching does not put an offside player onside.

front: What are the allowed methods for holding the ball for a kick off? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The ball may be held, placed on the ground, or placed on a tee, provided that the lowest point of the ball is not more than 1 inch (2.54 cm) above the ground.

front: From where must a kick off be made at the start of the first and third periods? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: From any point on or between the hash marks on Team A’s 45 yard (40 metre) line.

front: After Team A scores a field goal, what options does the team scored against have regarding the subsequent kick off? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The team scored against may elect to kick off or scrimmage from its own 35 yard (30 metre) line. Team A will kick off from its 45 yard (40 metre) line if the option is not taken.

front: How is the neutral zone defined on a kick off? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 2
back: The neutral zone on a kick off is the area from the line of kick off to the line 10 yards (10 metres) in advance of the line of kick off, from sideline to sideline.

front: What is the minimum distance the ball must be kicked towards the opponent's goal on a legal kick off, unless touched by an opponent? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: The ball must be kicked at least 10 yards (10 metres) toward the opponent’s goal.

front: What is the penalty if Team A illegally touches and recovers the ball on a kick off? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: Team B has the option of L5 kick off repeated, or B possession as 1D at the point of illegal touching, the point of recovery by Team A, or at the out-of-bounds point, or decline and take the result of the play.

front: What happens if a kick off goes out of bounds at the sideline without being touched by a player? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: Team B has the option of L5 kick off repeated, possession at the out-of-bounds point, or possession 25 yards in advance of point of kick off.

front: What happens if a kick off goes out of bounds in the end zone in flight without being touched by a player? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: The ball is immediately dead and Team B shall scrimmage at any point on or between the hash marks on its own 20 yard (20 metre) line, with no option.

front: When does Team A score 1 point on a kick off related to the end zone? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: If Team B fails to advance the ball out of the end zone, or the kick off lands inbounds, and then goes out of bounds in the end zone, Team A scores 1 point.

front: At the instant the ball is kicked off, which players of Team A are allowed to be in advance of the ball? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: Only the player who may be holding the ball for the kickoff or the kicker.

front: What is the penalty for Team A being offside on a kick off? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: L5, kick off repeated or L5 PBD.

front: What is the penalty if Team B players are in the neutral zone before the ball is kicked on a kick off? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: L5 to Team B, kick off repeated.

front: Under what conditions may Team B players interfere with an opponent on a kick off? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 5
back: Team B players may interfere with any opponent within bounds, after the ball is kicked, until it is declared dead, provided that the initial contact is made at or above the waist.

front: When is it illegal for Team A players to block on a kick off? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 5
back: Any form of blocking by Team A players is illegal interference, except when using hands and arms to ward off blockers or using bodies in blocking against players protecting the ball carrier, provided initial contact is at or above the waist.

front: What is the penalty for illegal interference by Team A when the ball is in flight during a kick off, if the foul is in an area remote from the point of possession and does not affect the gaining of possession by Team B? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 5
back: L10 PP (point of possession).

front: What is a 'Wedge Block' and what is its penalty? Rule 5 | Section 2 | Article 5
back: A 'Wedge Block' is when 3 or more players align shoulder to shoulder within 2 yards of each other and move forward in an attempt to block for a ball carrier. The penalty is L10 PBH (point behind the ball) or PP (point of possession).

front: What is the definition of a blocked kick from scrimmage? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: A blocked kick from scrimmage is when the ball, after being kicked, is prevented from crossing the line of scrimmage due to contact with an opponent or an offside Team A player. It is not a blocked kick if the ball then crosses the line of scrimmage after such contact.

front: How is a deflected kick different from a blocked kick? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: A deflected kick is when the ball, after being contacted by an opponent or offside Team A player, still crosses the line of scrimmage. The touching of the ball is disregarded for a deflected kick.

front: When is a return kick considered a blocked kick? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: A return kick is considered blocked when an opponent touches the ball simultaneously with or immediately after it is kicked, and the ball then travels parallel to or towards the kicking team's dead line. It is not a blocked kick if it travels towards the opponent's dead line after contact.

front: What happens if Team B legally recovers a blocked kick in bounds? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: If Team B legally recovers a blocked kick in bounds, it is Team B's 1st down at the point where the ball went dead (PBD).

front: What are the down consequences if Team A legally recovers a blocked kick in bounds on 1st or 2nd down? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: If Team A legally recovers a blocked kick in bounds on 1st or 2nd down, downs continue unless yards are gained.

front: Can Team A throw a forward pass after legally recovering a blocked kick? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: Yes, when Team A legally recovers a blocked kick, the continuing play is considered a normal play from scrimmage, and a forward pass may be thrown, subject to Rule 4, Section 3, Article 3.

front: Under what condition is a forward pass illegal after a blocked kick? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: If Team B recovers a blocked kick and then loses possession to Team A, a forward pass by either team is illegal, with the exception of a convert attempt.

front: What is the ruling if a blocked kick goes out of bounds in the field of play, and Team A last touched it on 1st or 2nd down? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: If a blocked kick goes out of bounds in the field of play, and Team A last touched it on 1st or 2nd down, possession is retained by Team A, downs continue unless the required distance is gained. The next down is 24 yards (22 metres) in from the sideline, at the point of last touching by A, or the point where the ball went out of bounds, whichever is closer to the A goal line.

front: What is the ruling if a blocked kick goes out of bounds in the field of play, and Team B last touched it? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: If a blocked kick goes out of bounds in the field of play, and Team B last touched it (on 1st, 2nd, or 3rd down), possession is awarded to Team B for a 1st down, 24 yards (22 metres) in from the sideline at the point of last touching by B, or at the point where the ball went out of bounds, whichever is closer to the B goal line.

front: How many points are awarded if a blocked kick goes dead in Team A's possession in the end zone or is last touched by A before going out of bounds in the end zone? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: 2 points (safety touch) are awarded to Team B.

front: What is the ruling if a blocked kick is directed into the end zone by a Team B player, and then goes dead in Team A's possession in the end zone? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: If a blocked kick is directed into the end zone from the field of play by a Team B player and goes dead in Team A's possession in the end zone, Team A gets 1st down at the 20-yard line (no score).

front: What is the ruling if a return kick by Team B is blocked by Team A in the B end zone, and the ball goes dead in B's possession in the B end zone? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: If a return kick by Team B is blocked by Team A in the B end zone, and the ball goes dead in B's possession in the B end zone, a score of 1 or 2 points, as appropriate, is awarded to Team A.

front: What is 'pyramiding' in football rules? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 5
back: Pyramiding is when a player uses the body of another player anywhere in bounds in any way to gain or maintain elevation on any play, or elevates a teammate in any way on any play.

front: What is the penalty for pyramiding? Rule 5 | Section 3 | Article 5
back: The penalty for pyramiding is L5 PLS (Loss of 5 yards, Previous Line of Scrimmage).

front: Under what condition does Article 1 – Offside beyond Line of Scrimmage (Restraining Zone Foul) not apply? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 1
back: This article does not apply to a dribbled ball, or to a kick which does not cross the line of scrimmage.

front: What is the penalty if an offside player touches or is touched by a kick from scrimmage beyond the line of scrimmage, a return kick, or an open-field kick? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 1 (a)
back: The penalty is L15 from the PBT (point ball touched) if in the field of play, or L15 applied at the 10-yard line if in the goal area.

front: How much distance must an offside player allow an opponent attempting to gain possession of a kicked ball? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 1 (b)
back: An offside player must allow 5 yards to an opponent attempting to gain possession of the kicked ball. The five-yard zone is a circle with a five-yard radius, centered on the ball at the instant it is first touched.

front: What is the penalty if an offside player does not allow 5 yards to an opponent attempting to gain possession of a kicked ball, and the ball strikes the ground before being touched by the receiving team? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 1 (b)
back: The penalty is L5 PBT or PBD if in the field of play, or L5 applied at the 10-yard line or PBD if in the goal area.

front: What is the penalty if a kicking team player makes no effort to withdraw from the 5-yard zone and hovers over the ball or receiving team player about to take possession? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 1 (c)
back: A L15 penalty will apply at the normal point of application regardless of whether the ball bounced.

front: What is the penalty if a kicking team player interferes with a receiving team player attempting to gain possession of a kicked ball, with or without contact? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 1 (d)
back: The penalty is L15 from the normal point of application.

front: When is a scrimmage kick or return kick whistled dead if it travels only a short distance? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (a)
back: A scrimmage kick which travels only a short distance across the line of scrimmage, or a short return kick (not including a dribbled ball), shall be whistled dead as soon as the ball touches a player or the ground, with possession awarded to the receiving team.

front: What happens if a short kick is whistled dead on the final play of a half? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (a)
back: The receiving team shall be entitled to 1 play from scrimmage if they so elect, with no distance penalty assessed.

front: When should a short kick not be whistled dead even if it travels only a short distance? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (b)
back: The ball should NOT be whistled dead if it is dropping into the end zone, or if it is a scrimmage kick or return kick from the end zone that does not leave the end zone.

front: What are the penalty options for the non-offending team if a restraining zone foul is committed on a scrimmage kick or return kick from the end zone that does not leave the end zone? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (b)
back: For a scrimmage kick, the option is 2 points or possession (1D at 10-yard line). For a return kick, the option is 1 point or possession (1D at 10-yard line).

front: When is an offside player penalized for Unnecessary Roughness (UR) or Rough Play (RP) in addition to a restraining zone foul? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (c)
back: An offside player who is within the restraining zone and contacts the receiver before he/she touches the ball shall be penalized for UR or RP, unless the contact was incidental and unavoidable in the opinion of the official.

front: Who may be the first player to legally enter the restraining zone to recover the ball? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (d)
back: The kicker or an onside player may be the first player to legally enter the restraining zone to recover the ball.

front: What contact is allowed by the kicker or onside player when recovering the ball in the restraining zone? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (d)
back: No contact shall be made with the opposing receiver, except in a legitimate attempt to recover the ball. All other contact is illegal.

front: What happens if the ball is motionless on the ground and the receiver feints as if to pick up the ball? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (e)
back: The receiver may be tackled without penalty.

front: If an offside player touches a motionless ball first after a receiver feints picking it up, who gets possession? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (e) (iii)
back: Possession is awarded to the receiving team at that point, with no distance penalty.

front: What is the penalty if a kicking team player illegally recovers or touches a scrimmage kick in the end zone before it is touched by an opponent, without attempting to allow an opponent to recover it? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (f)
back: There is no score, and it is the opponent’s ball, 1st down at the 35-yard line, or at the PLS if the ball entered the end zone as a result of a missed field goal where the PLS was outside the 35.

front: When can the receiving team choose to scrimmage at their own 20-yard line after a kick from scrimmage enters the end zone? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 2 (g)
back: They can choose to scrimmage at their own 20-yard line if they successfully advance the ball legally out of the end zone and retain possession without returning the ball into the end zone.

front: What happens if a kicked ball strikes the opponent’s goal post assembly in flight? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 3
back: The ball shall be dead immediately and awarded to the receiving team; 1st down, at any point on or between the hash marks on its 20-yard line.

front: Under what conditions does a kicked ball striking the goal post assembly remain in play? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 3
back: A kicked ball remains in play if it strikes the opponent’s goal post assembly after striking the ground, a player, or an official, or if it strikes the kicking team’s goal post assembly.

front: When does a score count on a field goal or convert attempt even if the ball strikes the goal post assembly? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 4
back: The score shall count if the ball strikes the goal post assembly but still goes over the crossbar and between the uprights.

front: Where is the ball put into play after a missed field goal? Rule 5 | Section 4 | Article 4 (a)
back: At any point between the hash marks on the 20-yard line.

front: Under what conditions can players of the receiving team interfere with players of the kicking team who have crossed the line of scrimmage on a scrimmage kick? Rule 5 | Section 5 | Article 1a
back: Players of the receiving team may interfere with any player of the kicking team who has crossed the line of scrimmage, provided that the initial contact is made at or above the waist. This interference is legal from the time the ball is snapped until it is declared dead.

front: What is the penalty application if the receiving team commits interference on a scrimmage kick while the ball is in flight? Rule 5 | Section 5 | Article 1a
back: The penalty is applied at the Point of Possession. Unnecessary Roughness or Rough Play will be applied at the Point of Possession or PBD (except against the kicker, where it can be PP, PBD, or PLS at the option of Team A).

front: What is the penalty for interference against the kicker behind the neutral zone on a scrimmage kick, if not a quick kick? Rule 5 | Section 5 | Article 1a
back: The penalty is 1.2.3D – L10 PP.

front: When does the kicker lose protection from interference behind the neutral zone on a scrimmage kick? Rule 5 | Section 5 | Article 1b
back: The kicker loses this protection once the receiving team has touched the ball, or if it is a quick kick.

front: When can players of the team receiving a return kick interfere with opponents, including the kicker? Rule 5 | Section 5 | Article 2
back: Players of the team receiving a return kick may interfere with any opponent, including the kicker, from the time the ball is kicked, provided that the initial contact is made at or above the waist, until the ball is declared dead.

front: What is the penalty application if the receiving team commits interference on a return kick after gaining possession? Rule 5 | Section 5 | Article 2
back: The penalty is applied at the PBH. Unnecessary Roughness or Rough Play will be applied at the PBH or PBD.

front: What are the legal actions for players of the kicking team during a kick play regarding blocking and interference? Rule 5 | Section 5 | Article 3
back: Players of the kicking team may block any opponent up to the limit of the neutral zone, use their hands and arms to ward off blockers interfering with their approach to the ball carrier while proceeding downfield, and use their bodies in blocking against players protecting the ball carrier, provided that the initial contact is made at or above the waist.

front: What is the penalty for illegal interference by the kicking team when the ball is in flight? Rule 5 | Section 5 | Article 3
back: The penalty is L10 PP.

front: When can all players of the kicking team legally interfere with opponents after a kick? Rule 5 | Section 5 | Article 4
back: If the kicker or an onside player legally recovers the kick, all players of that team may legally interfere with the opponents after such recovery, provided that the initial contact is at or above the waist.

front: When a penalty in Rule 5, Section 5 is applied from the 10-yard (10-meter) line, where may Team A scrimmage the ball? Rule 5 | Section 5 | Article 5
back: Team A may scrimmage the ball at any point on or between the hash marks, on the line where the ball is placed after the penalty application.

front: What defines a 'Dribbled ball'? Rule 5 | Section 6 | Article: Dribbled Ball
back: A dribbled ball occurs by kicking the ball when it is loose (not in possession of any player).

front: Who may touch a dribbled ball without penalty? Rule 5 | Section 6 | Article: Dribbled Ball
back: A dribbled ball may be touched by the kicker or any onside player without penalty.

front: What is the effect if an opponent touches a dribbled ball? Rule 5 | Section 6 | Article: Dribbled Ball
back: If a dribbled ball is touched by the opponent, all offside players become onside.

front: What is the penalty if an offside player touches a dribbled ball? Rule 5 | Section 6 | Article: Dribbled Ball
back: Award ball to the opponent at point of touch, or option.

front: What is the penalty if an offside player touches a dribbled ball in the opponent's Goal Area? Rule 5 | Section 6 | Article: Dribbled Ball
back: Award ball to opponent at their 20 yard (20 metre) line, or option.

front: What is the penalty if an offside player touches a dribbled ball in their own Goal Area? Rule 5 | Section 6 | Article: Dribbled Ball
back: Accept a score of 1 or 2 points as applicable, or take possession of the ball as 1st down at the PLS or 10 yard (10 metre line whichever is closer to the opponent’s goal line.

front: What happens if an offside player's touching of a dribbled ball occurs on the last play of a half? Rule 5 | Section 6 | Article: Dribbled Ball
back: The opponent may elect to extend the period for an additional play, from point of touch.

front: What is the definition of a lateral or onside pass? Rule 6 | Section 1 – Lateral Or Onside Pass
back: A lateral or onside pass is one thrown, handed, knocked, batted, or fumbled by a player parallel to or in the direction of their own deadline.

front: What factor determines whether a pass is considered a lateral pass? Rule 6 | Section 1 – Lateral Or Onside Pass
back: The point of termination is the factor that determines whether it is a lateral pass. This is the point at which the ball is caught, strikes another player, an official, or the ground, or goes out of bounds.

front: What is the status of a lateral pass that strikes the ground? Rule 6 | Section 1 – Lateral Or Onside Pass
back: A lateral pass striking the ground is not dead and may be recovered legally by either team.

front: Where is the ball put into play when a lateral pass goes out of bounds without being touched by a player after the pass is made? Rule 6 | Section 1 – Lateral Or Onside Pass
back: The ball shall be put into play at the hash mark at the out of bounds point, or at the point of origin of the pass, whichever is closer to the dead line of the team entitled to possession.

front: What defines a Hand Off Pass on a scrimmage play? Rule 6 | Section 2 - HAND OFF PASS
back: A Hand Off Pass is made on a scrimmage play, when the ball is handed in any direction but not thrown, by one Team A player to another, behind the line of scrimmage.

front: What positional restriction applies to the player receiving a Hand Off Pass? Rule 6 | Section 2 - HAND OFF PASS
back: The player receiving the pass must not at that point be occupying the position of a lineman.

front: Are there any limits on the number of Hand Off Passes permitted on a single play? Rule 6 | Section 2 - HAND OFF PASS
back: There are no restrictions on the number of hand off passes on any one play.

front: Under what condition is a hand off pass in a forward direction considered illegal? Rule 6 | Section 2 - HAND OFF PASS
back: A hand off pass in a forward direction is illegal following a completed Forward Pass.

front: What is the definition of an offside pass? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: An offside pass is made when the ball is directed in any manner other than being kicked, in the direction of the opponent’s dead line.

front: What is the penalty for a team making an illegal recovery after an offside pass? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: The penalty is the next scrimmage at the point of origin of the pass or the option to take the penalty.

front: What are the exceptions to the illegal recovery rule for an offside pass? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: Exceptions include a handoff pass behind the line of scrimmage or a forward pass.

front: Under what general conditions does an offside pass occur on a scrimmage play? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: On a scrimmage play, an offside pass occurs when a Team A player makes an offside pass after he/she has crossed the line of scrimmage.

front: When does an offside pass generally occur after a change of possession? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: An offside pass generally occurs after a change of possession (e.g., punt runback, fumble recovery, intercepted pass) if a player makes an offside pass.

front: What constitutes an offside pass during an attempted forward pass if an ineligible receiver catches the ball? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: If, in attempting to complete a forward pass, a Team A eligible receiver tips, deflects, knocks, or bats the ball in an offside direction where it is caught by a Team A ineligible receiver, it is an offside pass.

front: What is the penalty for an offside pass in the general occurrence situations outlined in Article 3? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: The penalty is the next scrimmage at the point of origin of the offside pass, and downs continue, unless the required distance has been gained at that point.

front: When does an offside pass NOT occur on a scrimmage play before the ball crosses the line of scrimmage? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: An offside pass does NOT occur when, on a scrimmage play, before the ball has crossed the line of scrimmage, a Team A player throws an offside pass – this is ruled as a forward pass.

front: Under what conditions is a tipped ball in an offside direction by an eligible receiver NOT considered an offside pass? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: It is NOT an offside pass if, in attempting to complete a forward pass, a Team A eligible receiver tips, deflects, knocks, or bats the ball in an offside direction, where it is caught by another Team A eligible receiver.

front: When is a tipped ball by a Team B player during an attempted interception NOT considered an offside pass? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: It is NOT an offside pass if, in attempting to intercept a forward pass, a Team B player tips, deflects, knocks or bats the ball in an offside direction where it is caught by another Team B player.

front: What is the ruling when a Team A passer crosses the line of scrimmage and throws what the Referee considers an intentional forward pass? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: This shall be ruled as an illegal forward pass. The penalty is 1, 2, 3D – L10 DR; Convert – L10 DR.

front: In what specific fumbled ball situations does an offside pass NOT occur? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 4
back: An offside pass does NOT occur on a ball fumbled forward by a ball carrier, or a player attempting to catch a kicked ball, or by a player attempting to intercept a lateral pass.

front: What is the ruling when the ball is fumbled forward from the field of play directly to out-of-bounds? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 5
back: The ball shall be scrimmaged at the point of origin of the fumble and downs continue, unless the required distance is gained at that point. This applies whether the out-of-bounds spot is in the field of play or the end zone.

front: How is a ball fumbled forward by Team A into the Team B end zone, and recovered by Team B, ruled? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 6
back: It shall be ruled as an intercepted forward pass.

front: Under what condition may a ball thrown in an offside direction be legally recovered by the throwing team? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 7
back: The ball may not be recovered legally by the throwing team unless it meets the requirements of a Forward Pass.

front: What is the penalty if a ball thrown in an offside direction is not legally recovered by the throwing team? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 7
back: The penalty is the next scrimmage at the point of origin of the offside pass, and downs continue, unless the required distance is gained at that point.

front: What is the outcome if Team A makes an offside pass in its own end zone and retains possession? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 8
back: Team B shall be awarded 2 points or option.

front: What is the outcome if Team B makes an offside pass in its own end zone and retains possession after receiving a Team A kick? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 8
back: Team A shall be awarded 1 point or option.

front: What is the outcome if Team B makes an offside pass in its own end zone and retains possession while or after intercepting a Team A forward pass? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 8
back: Team B shall scrimmage at any point on or between the hash marks on its own 20 yard (20 metre) line, or at PBD (Team A option). No score.

front: What are Team B's options if Team A fumbles the ball from the end zone to out of bounds in the field of play without touching an opponent on 1st or 2nd down? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 8
back: Team B has the choice of 2 options: 1. 2 points for a safety touch. 2. Allow A to scrimmage on the hash mark at the out of bounds spot, downs continue.

front: What are Team B's options if Team A fumbles the ball from the end zone to out of bounds in the field of play without touching an opponent on 3rd down? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 8
back: Team B has the choice of 2 options: 1. 2 points for a safety touch. 2. 1st Down for B on the hash mark at the out of bounds spot.

front: Why is a fumble from the end zone to out of bounds in the field of play, not touching an opponent, considered an offside pass in the end zone? Rule 6 | Section 3 | Article 8
back: It is considered an offside pass because the point of termination is closer to the opponent’s dead line than the point of the pass.

front: What defines a forward pass in football? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 1 – DEFINITION
back: A forward pass is thrown by any Team A player from behind the line of scrimmage toward the Team B dead line, to any eligible receiver, without touching the ground, goal post assembly, an official, or going out of bounds.

front: Under what condition is a forward pass considered illegal after a change of possession? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 1 – DEFINITION
back: A forward pass is illegal after a change of possession by either team. If Team B gains possession from a fumble, blocked kick, etc., and subsequently loses possession again to Team A, a forward pass by either team is illegal.

front: How many forward passes are allowed on each down? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 2 – NUMBER OF FORWARD PASSES
back: A forward pass shall be thrown once only on each down. A second forward pass on the same down shall be penalized with L10 DR.

front: Who can throw a forward pass for Team A? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 3 – PASSER
back: Any Team A player who is behind the line of scrimmage when they throw the ball may be the passer. The passer need not be the first player to receive the ball from the centre.

front: Who are considered eligible receivers for a forward pass? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 4 – ELIGIBLE RECEIVERS
back: Eligible receivers include: players at each end of the scrimmage line at the snap wearing numbers 0-49 or 80-99; players clearly back of the scrimmage line at the snap wearing numbers 0-49 or 80-99; a Team A player wearing numbers 0-49 or 80-99 who is in forward motion from a backfield position and within one yard of the line of scrimmage at the snap; all players of Team B; and all players of Team A if the ball is touched by a B player.

front: Who are considered ineligible receivers for Team A? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 5 – INELIGIBLE RECEIVERS
back: Players of Team A wearing numbers 50-79 are ineligible receivers, regardless of their position, unless declared eligible as indicated by rule 4-3-1.

front: What is the penalty for an ineligible receiver being the first Team A player to catch or touch the ball? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 5 – INELIGIBLE RECEIVERS
back: The penalty is 1.2D – L10 DR, 3D DG – L10 DR, DNG – LB PLS or PBD.

front: Under what conditions can an ineligible receiver go downfield beyond the neutral zone? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 5 – INELIGIBLE RECEIVERS
back: An ineligible receiver can go downfield beyond the neutral zone only if they make contact with an opponent in the neutral zone and maintain this contact as they move downfield.

front: When is a forward pass considered complete when caught by Team A? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 6 – COMPLETED FORWARD PASS
back: A forward pass is complete when caught inbounds by a Team A eligible receiver, or simultaneously by two or more Team A eligible receivers, and the player maintains complete and continuous control of the ball throughout the process of contacting the ground.

front: What happens if a forward pass is caught simultaneously by eligible receivers of both teams? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 6 – COMPLETED FORWARD PASS
back: The ball shall be awarded to Team A, even if it has been touched previously by Team B.

front: When is a forward pass ruled incomplete? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 7 – INCOMPLETE FORWARD PASS
back: A forward pass is incomplete when the ball touches the ground, goal post assembly, an official, a corner marker, Downsbox marker or yardstick assembly, or goes out of bounds, even if previously touched by a player. It is also incomplete when an eligible receiver catches a pass while off the ground, inbounds, and lands on or outside a boundary line.

front: What constitutes intentional grounding by Team A's passer? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 8 – INTENTIONAL GROUNDING
back: Intentional grounding occurs if Team A passer deliberately throws a forward pass that lands behind the line of scrimmage or Out of Bounds behind the line of scrimmage and to an area in which there is no eligible Team A receiver, to avoid a loss of yards.

front: What is the penalty for intentional grounding from the Goal Area? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 8 – INTENTIONAL GROUNDING
back: If the pass was thrown from the Goal Area, a safety touch score shall be awarded to Team B, subject to the right of Team B to decline the score and accept the play as it terminated.

front: When can a Team A player initiate contact with or block a Team B player more than 1 yard in advance of the line of scrimmage on a forward pass play? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 9 – INTERFERENCE
back: A Team A player may not initiate contact with or block a Team B player more than 1 yard in advance of the line of scrimmage until the pass has been touched by an eligible receiver.

front: When can Team B players interfere with Team A players behind the neutral zone? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 9 – INTERFERENCE
back: Team B players may interfere with any Team A player behind the neutral zone who is protecting the passer.

front: Under what condition is contact between two opponents legal when a pass is in the air? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 9 – INTERFERENCE
back: Contact is legal if it results from a simultaneous and bonafide attempt to play the ball at the spot of possible completion, where each player is intent on playing the ball, contact is unavoidable and incidental, and each player is in an equally favourable position to play the ball.

front: What defines illegal interference on a forward pass? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 10 – ILLEGAL INTERFERENCE PENALTIES
back: Illegal interference is interference with an eligible receiver in the target area, or interference which prevented an eligible receiver from reaching the target area, when there is a reasonable expectation that the receiver would have had the opportunity to attempt to complete the pass.

front: What is the penalty for illegal interference by Team B across the line of scrimmage? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 10 – ILLEGAL INTERFERENCE PENALTIES
back: The penalty is 1D at PF if less than 15 yards in advance of the PLS, or 1D plus 15 from the PLS if the PF is more than 15 yards in advance of the PLS.

front: What happens if a Team A player fumbles the ball forward into the Team B end zone and Team B recovers it? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 11 – INTERCEPTION IN THE END ZONE
back: It shall be ruled as an intercepted pass.

front: If Team B intercepts a pass in the end zone and the ball goes dead in their possession without being advanced, what is the result? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 11 – INTERCEPTION IN THE END ZONE
back: There is no score. Team B shall scrimmage at any point between the hash marks on their 20 yard (20 metre) line.

front: When is a dropped ball by the passer ruled an incomplete pass versus a fumble? Rule 6 | Section 4 | Article 12 – MISCELLANEOUS
back: If the passer is contacted after starting the passing motion and the ball is dropped, it is an incomplete pass. If contacted before starting passing motion and the ball is dropped, it is a fumble.

front: What is the definition of holding in the context of Fouls and Penalties? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 1
back: Holding is the use of the hands and/or arms to grasp or encircle an opponent, except when a player tackles the ball carrier, and is illegal if the hold has an impact on the play.

front: What is the penalty for Team A committing a holding foul on 1st or 2nd down? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 1
back: The penalty for Team A is L10 DR (loss of 10 yards, down repeated).

front: Under what conditions is the use of hands and arms permitted by a ball carrier? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 1
back: The use of hands and arms is permitted by the ball carrier to ward off an opponent.

front: When is the use of hands and arms permitted for a defender? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 1
back: The use of hands and arms is permitted by a defender to reach the ball carrier, but the hands may not be used to grasp any opponent except the ball carrier.

front: What actions constitute illegal use of hands by blocking an opponent? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 2
back: Blocking an opponent by pushing him/her from the rear with extended arms or bumping him/her above the waist from behind is illegal and defined as illegal use of hands.

front: What is the penalty for Team B committing illegal use of hands when the play results in a gain of ground (DG)? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 2
back: The penalty for Team B is L10 PBH (loss of 10 yards, penalty enforced from the spot of the foul).

front: How is tripping defined? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 3
back: Tripping is the intentional use of the lower leg or foot to obstruct any opponent below the knee.

front: Under what circumstances is contacting the kicker, while in the act of kicking, illegal? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 4
back: Contacting the kicker, while in the act of kicking, is illegal unless the contact is slight and incidental.

front: When does the act of kicking begin and end for the purpose of kicker protection? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 4
back: The act of kicking begins when the kicking foot leaves the ground and ends when the foot returns to the ground (or a player lying on the ground) after kicking or attempting to kick the ball.

front: What is the penalty for illegally contacting the kicker? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 4
back: The penalty for illegally contacting the kicker is L10 PLS (loss of 10 yards, penalty enforced from the previous line of scrimmage).

front: Under what conditions is a player not penalized for contacting the kicker? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 4
back: A player shall not be penalized if they block or touch the ball prior to contacting the kicker, or if contact by a Team A blocker causes contact with the kicker, or if a B player contacts an A player in such a way as to drive the player into the kicker.

front: What type of deceptive tactics are considered illegal? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 5
back: The use of tactics to deceive opponents such as the alleged need for equipment (e.g., a tee, mouthguard) or the pretence of calling players toward the bench as if a time out had been called, is illegal.

front: What is the penalty for using illegal deceptive tactics on 1st or 2nd down? Rule 7 | Fouls and Penalties | Article 5
back: The penalty is L5 DR (loss of 5 yards, down repeated).

front: What constitutes rough play regarding charging a kicker, passer, or receiver? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 1
back: The deliberate charging of a kicker, passer, or receiver of a kick or pass in such a way as to cause calculated injury.

front: Which actions are considered rough play when striking an opponent? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 2
back: The striking of an opponent with the fist, heel of the hand, knee or elbow, or kicking an opponent.

front: Under what condition can head leading blocking, tackling, or spearing be penalized as rough play? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 3
back: Head leading blocking, head leading tackling or spearing, if done deliberately in such a way as to cause calculated injury may be penalized under this section.

front: When can grasping the helmet be penalized as rough play? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 4
back: Grasping the helmet, if in the opinion of the Official it was a deliberate attempt to injure an opponent, may be penalized under this section.

front: What is the penalty for rough play outlined in Articles 1 to 6? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 5
back: Disqualification of the offending player, and L25 from the appropriate point as covered in Rule 8, Section 5. Automatic 1D to Team A for Team B Rough Play.

front: What happens if the official cannot identify the offender for rough play? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 5
back: If the official is unable to identify the offender, the distance penalty only shall be applied.

front: What happens if both teams commit rough play? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 5
back: If both teams offend, the players involved shall be disqualified but no distance penalty shall be applied. Play shall be resumed at the appropriate point as outlined in Dual Penalties. Rule 8, Section 6.

front: What is prohibited regarding targeting and making forcible contact to an opponent's head or neck area? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 6
back: No player shall target and make forcible contact to the head or neck area of an opponent with the helmet, forearm, hand, fist, elbow or shoulder. This foul requires at least one indicator of targeting.

front: What does "Targeting" mean? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 6
back: "Targeting" means that a player takes aim at an opponent for purposes of attacking with forcible contact that goes beyond making a legal tackle or a legal block or playing the ball.

front: What are some indicators of targeting? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 6
back: Indicators of targeting include: 1) Launch – a player leaving their feet to attack an opponent by an upward and forward thrust of the body to make forcible contact in the head or neck area 2) A crouch followed by an upward and forward thrust to attack with forcible contact at the head or neck area 3) Leading with helmet, shoulder, forearm, fist, hand or elbow to attack with forcible contact at the head or neck area 4) Lowering the head before attacking by initiating forcible contact with the crown of the helmet.

front: What is the penalty for targeting and making forcible contact to the head or neck area? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 6
back: L25 Player Disqualified from game. For Levels U14 and below, the player will receive a warning for the first offense.

front: Under what conditions is a player disqualified from further participation in the game? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 7
back: A player is disqualified if: a) the player has been called for Rough play b) the player has been called for physical abuse of an official.

front: Can the non-offending team decline a disqualification penalty? Rule 7 | Rough Play | Article 7
back: No, the disqualification penalty cannot be declined by the non-offending team.

front: How many Unnecessary Roughness penalties result in a player's disqualification from the game? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness
back: A player will be disqualified after receiving a third Unnecessary Roughness penalty.

front: What action constitutes 'piling on' in football? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 1
back: Piling on occurs when a player runs into, throws their body against, or falls upon a ball carrier after the play has been terminated by the official's whistle, or when the ball is clearly dead, including tackling a player out of bounds or throwing a dead ball carrier to the ground.

front: What is required of a player in possession of the ball when sliding to give up? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 1
back: When a player in possession of the ball is giving up by sliding, all unnecessary contact must be avoided, and the slide must be done in a timely manner to allow the defense to avoid such contact.

front: Under what conditions is a defender prohibited from hitting a passer in the knee area or below? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 2
back: A defender is prohibited from forcibly hitting a passer in the knee area or below who has one or both feet planted on the ground, even if the initial contact is above the knee, unless the defender is blocked (or fouled) into the passer and has no opportunity to avoid contact, or is swiping, wrapping, or grabbing in an attempt to tackle.

front: What actions are prohibited when a defender tackles a passer after the ball has been thrown? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 2
back: A defender is prohibited from intimidating and punishing acts such as stuffing a passer to the ground, or unnecessarily wrestling or driving them down and landing on top with all or most of the defender's weight after the ball has been thrown. Instead, the defender must strive to wrap up the passer with their arms.

front: What contact with a passer's head or neck area is prohibited for a defender? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 2
back: A defender is prohibited from using the helmet and/or facemask to hit the passer, or using hands, arms, or other parts of the body forcibly in the head or neck area.

front: When can a player still be called for Roughing the Kicker even if they touch the ball first? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 3
back: A player can still be called for Roughing the Kicker if they touch the ball prior to contacting the kicker's plant leg.

front: What protection is afforded to a place kick holder during a field goal or convert attempt? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 4
back: The holder of a place kick for a field goal or convert attempt shall be given the same protection as a kicker.

front: What actions are illegal regarding an opponent's helmet? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 5
back: It is illegal to grasp the helmet of an opponent by closing the fingers on the face mask, chin strap, or other helmet opening (ear holes).

front: What is meant by 'clotheslining' in the context of tackling, and is it legal? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 6
back: 'Clotheslining' refers to tackling around the head in the open field, or a straight arm tackle to the head, and it is illegal.

front: What is 'spearing' and when is a player called for it? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 7
back: Spearing is driving the helmet into a player who is down, going down, whose forward progress has been stopped, or who is unable to protect themselves. A player is called for spearing even if before the ball is dead, if using the head and helmet as the primary point of force.

front: What constitutes a 'Head Leading Block'? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 8
back: A Head Leading Block is when any player, including the ball carrier, uses the helmet to butt or ram an opponent.

front: What constitutes a 'Head Leading Tackle'? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 8
back: A Head Leading Tackle is when any player strikes the runner with the crown or top of the helmet.

front: When is the use of hands and arms considered unnecessary roughness? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 9
back: The use of hands and arms is unnecessary roughness if contact is made with the fist, heel of the hand, or elbow, if the blocking arm is cocked by swinging back of the body line prior to contact, if the blocking arm is driven upward and forward in an 'elbow smash' manner, if the blocker turns their body at the waist or pivots to add force to the blow, if contact is made with clasped hands, or if the opponent is struck above the shoulder with the hand or arm in an unnecessarily rough manner including a 'head slap'.

front: Under what conditions is a 'Crack-Back Block' illegal for a Team A player? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 10
back: A 'Crack-Back Block' is illegal if a Team A player blocks an opponent below the waist or delivers a forcible block in the area from 5 yards ahead of the line of scrimmage, sideline to sideline, extending back to the Team A deadline, AND the A player is stationed or in motion 3+ yards outside the Block Below the Waist Area at the snap; OR stationed initially 3+ yards outside and moves toward the ball to be less than 3 yards from the area at the snap; OR stationed initially less than 3 yards from the area, moves more than 3 yards away, and then returns to less than 3 yards from the area, AND moves in the direction of the ball to make the block.

front: When is a Team A player not penalized for a crack-back block, even if moving into the Block Below the Waist Area? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 10
back: If the Team A player moves into the Block Below the Waist Area prior to the snap and comes to a complete stop, the player shall not be penalized for a crack-back block.

front: What is a 'Delayed Knee Blocking' foul? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 11
back: Delayed Knee Blocking is when a player blocks an opponent, at or below the knees, at the time that the opponent is already being engaged by a teammate of the blocker, with or without physical contact.

front: What protection is given to the center on kick plays from scrimmage? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 12
back: On all kick plays from scrimmage (punts, field goal attempts, and converts), it is illegal to contact the center on, or within one yard either side of, the line of scrimmage.

front: Is hurdling the center to avoid contact permissible on kick plays? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 12
back: No, hurdling the center in an attempt to avoid contact is not permissible and is penalized the same as if there was contact, with the exception of a quick kick.

front: What actions constitute a 'Horse Collar' foul? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 13
back: A 'Horse Collar' foul is grasping an opponent by the inside of the shoulder pads, or by the inside collar of the jersey, or grasping the outside of the jersey above the numbers and using this as the primary means of causing a change in the ball carrier’s direction.

front: When is an 'Illegal Block, Hands to Face' penalized? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 14
back: An 'Illegal Block, Hands to Face' is penalized when any player forcibly thrusts their hands forward above the frame to contact an opponent on the neck, face, head, or facemask. It is also a penalty if the initial contact is to the chest but the hands ride up to the neck, face, head, or facemask and the contact is forcible or prolonged.

front: What is 'Blocking from the Rear'? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 15
back: 'Blocking from the Rear' is blocking an opponent, other than the ball carrier, from the rear by charging into the opponent’s back with the body, or throwing the body across the back of the legs.

front: When is 'Blocking from the Rear' considered legal? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 15
back: Blocking from the rear is legal if: 1) the block occurs in the Close Line Play area, is made by a player positioned in this area at the snap, and the contact is above the waist; OR 2) the initial point of contact is on the side or front of the opponent; OR 3) the initial point of contact is from the rear due to the opponent turning their back on the blocker after the blocker has committed to the block.

front: Who is considered a player in a defenseless posture? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 16
back: Players in a defenseless posture include: a player in the act of or just after throwing a pass; a receiver attempting to catch a pass or who has completed a catch and not had time to protect themselves or become a runner; a runner in the grasp of a tackler with forward progress stopped; a player attempting to field a kick in the air; a player on the ground; a kicker/punter during the kick or return; a quarterback after a change of possession; a player receiving a block when the blocker is moving toward or parallel to their own end line and approaches from behind or side; and a player protected from an illegal crack block.

front: What types of contact are prohibited against a player in a defenseless posture? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 16
back: Prohibited contact includes: forcibly hitting the defenseless player’s head or neck area with the helmet, facemask, forearm, or shoulder; lowering the head and making forcible contact with the top/crown or forehead/“hairline” parts of the helmet against any part of the defenseless player’s body; or illegally launching into a defenseless opponent by leaving both feet prior to contact to spring forward and upward and using any part of the helmet to initiate forcible contact.

front: What is the penalty for unnecessary roughness against a player in a defenseless posture? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 16
back: The penalty is a loss of 15 yards and an automatic first down. The player may be disqualified if the action is judged by the official(s) to be flagrant.

front: What defines an illegal 'Blindside Block'? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 17
back: An illegal 'Blindside Block' is a forcible block delivered by any player on an opponent while moving back towards or parallel to their own dead ball line anywhere on the field.

front: What are 'Tourist Hits' and when are they penalized? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 18
back: 'Tourist Hits' are unnecessary physical contact, such as running into, diving into, cut blocking, or throwing one's body on a player who is out of the play or would not have reasonably anticipated such contact, either before or after the ball is dead. Players are expected to know when the play is dead and if their actions are reasonable.

front: Under what specific conditions is blocking an opponent below the waist considered legal? Rule 7 | Section: Unnecessary Roughness | Article: 19
back: Blocking an opponent below the waist is legal only when the block occurs in the block below the waist area, is made by a player positioned in this area at the snap of the ball, and the block is above the knee. A player coming from outside this zone must come to a complete stop in the zone prior to the snap to be considered positioned in it.

front: What types of language or gestures are prohibited for players or team bench occupants towards opponents, officials, or spectators? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 1
back: The use of profane, obscene, or insulting language or gestures is prohibited.

front: What actions are considered unsportsmanlike conduct and prohibited under Objectionable Conduct? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 1
back: Throwing the ball at an opponent, an official, or occupant of the team bench is prohibited.

front: What tactics by players that delay or hinder the game's smooth operation are penalized under Objectionable Conduct? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 1
back: These tactics include spiking the ball, and/or deliberately throwing or kicking the ball away after it has been declared dead on a play.

front: What is the penalty for an objectionable conduct foul that occurs before the Referee has whistled time in for any down? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 1
back: The penalty is L10 from the point where the ball would have been put into play if no other foul occurred, or added to the penalty for any other foul.

front: What is the penalty for an objectionable conduct foul called after the Referee has whistled time in for any down? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 1
back: The penalty will be L10 PLS DR, and the distance chains will not be moved (unless a first down is gained from a penalty against Team B).

front: Under what condition may a player or occupant of the bench be disqualified for an objectionable conduct foul without a distance penalty? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 1
back: If the foul is of a serious nature, the player or occupant of the bench may be disqualified with no distance penalty.

front: What happens if a player throws a punch at an opponent, without contact? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 1
back: It is considered Objectionable Conduct.

front: When is a coach considered a player in relation to Objectionable Conduct rules? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 1
back: A coach who is playing with the team shall be considered as a player when on the field.

front: What is the consequence if a player, coach, or any member of a team is assessed a second Objectionable Conduct penalty during a game? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 1
back: The offending individual shall be removed from play.

front: What is the penalty for any player, team official, or bench occupant who engages in verbal taunts, insults, or intimidation based on Discriminatory Grounds? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 2
back: In addition to an objectionable conduct penalty, they shall be disqualified for the remainder of the game.

front: What are some examples of Discriminatory Grounds? Rule 7 | Objectionable Conduct | Article 2
back: Discriminatory Grounds include, but are not limited to: Race, national or ethnic origin, skin color, or language spoken; Religion, Faith, Beliefs; Age; Sex, Sexual Orientation, or Gender Identify/Expression; Marital or Familial Status; Genetic Characteristics; Disability.

front: What is the subject of Rule 8? Rule 8
back: Application of Penalties

front: What are the categories of penalties in this rulebook? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 1
back: Penalties shall fall into the following categories: Loss of Down, Loss of distance, Option Penalties, Penalties after legal gains, Restricted Penalties, Penalties in end zone, Disqualification, Unnecessary Roughness and Rough Play Penalties, and Dual and Double Penalties.

front: What does 'Loss of a Down' (LD) signify in the context of a penalty? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 2
back: Loss of a down (LD) means that the down upon which the foul occurred has used up one of the series of 3 consecutive downs permitted.

front: When a distance penalty is assessed for a foul, is there typically a loss of down as well? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 3
back: For any foul calling for a distance penalty, there shall be no loss of down.

front: What are the exceptions to the rule that distance penalties do not incur a loss of down? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 3
back: Exceptions to no loss of down for distance penalties are: Unnecessary Roughness, Rough Play, Objectionable Conduct, and Playing without a mouthguard.

front: What choice does the non-offending team have when a foul has been committed? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: The non-offending team shall be entitled to the penalty, or the option of declining the penalty to take any advantage of field position, score, down, time, etc.

front: Can the non-offending team decline a score to accept a penalty? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: Yes, the non-offending team may decline a score to accept a penalty, or may decline a penalty to allow a score in order to gain an advantage from field position, or may allow a score to gain an advantage from a better point of application of a penalty such as UR.

front: Under what circumstances is a penalty applied without the necessity of choosing an option? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: In certain cases, where so stated, a penalty shall be applied without the necessity of choosing an option. These cases include fouls such as Unnecessary Roughness, Rough Play, Objectionable Conduct, and No Mouthguard.

front: Can a team decline the distance for any penalty? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: Yes, a team may decline the distance for any penalty, including those where the penalty is applied without option, if they feel the application of the distance would not be advantageous to them.

front: When can the non-offending team decline a penalty to terminate a period? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: The non-offending team may decline the penalty for any foul which occurs after the ball has been snapped, during the final play of a period, in order to terminate the period.

front: Can a captain revoke their choice after accepting or declining a penalty option? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: No, once the captain entitled to the option has made the choice of accepting or declining the penalty, the choice may not be revoked.

front: When dual fouls occur, can one or both penalties be refused? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: Yes, when dual fouls occur, one or both penalties may be refused, with the exception of Unnecessary Roughness, Rough Play, Objectionable Conduct, and No Mouthguard.

front: Who is given the first option when dual fouls occur? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: The first option shall be given to the team against whom the first foul occurred.

front: Can the non-offending team decline a disqualification penalty? Rule 8 | Section 1 | Article 4
back: No, the disqualification penalty cannot be declined by the non-offending team, but immediate legal substitution is permitted.

front: When Team A commits a foul on a scrimmage play after legally gaining a first down, where is the penalty applied from and what is the down after the penalty? Rule 8 | Section 2 | Article 1
back: The penalty is applied from where the ball was held when the foul occurred. A first down is awarded at the point where the ball is placed after the penalty, with 10 yards to go.

front: If Team A commits a foul on a scrimmage play before gaining a first down, where is the penalty applied from and what is the down after the penalty? Rule 8 | Section 2 | Article 2
back: The penalty is applied from the point of last scrimmage, and the down is repeated.

front: When a team gains possession through an interception, recovered fumble, or received kick and then commits a foul, where is the penalty applied from and what is the down after the penalty? Rule 8 | Section 2 | Article 3
back: The penalty is applied from the point where the ball was held when the foul occurred, and 1st and 10 will be awarded at the point where the ball is placed after the penalty application.

front: How is a penalty applied if either team commits a foul while a kicked ball is "in flight"? Rule 8 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: The penalty is applied at the point of possession by the team which legally gains possession. Penalties normally applied without option may be applied at PBD at the option of the non-offending team.

front: What is the consequence if a foul on a loose ball directly affects its recovery? Rule 8 | Section 2 | Article 4
back: The ball will be awarded to the non-offending team at the PF, and an automatic 1st down. If the point of possession is the end zone, the penalty is applied from the 10-yard (10-meter) line.

front: What fouls are ignored if committed after the ball is dead? Rule 8 | Section 2 | Article 5
back: Fouls committed after the ball is dead are ignored unless they are Rough Play, Unnecessary Roughness, or Objectionable Conduct.

front: If Rough Play, Unnecessary Roughness, or Objectionable Conduct occurs after a score, how is it applied? Rule 8 | Section 2 | Article 5
back: The score shall count, and the foul will be applied on the subsequent scrimmage play, convert, or kick off at the option of the non-offending team. There is no option to decline the score.

front: When a yardage penalty is applied within 30 yards of the offending team's goal line, what is the maximum distance the penalty can be? Rule 8 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: The penalty shall not exceed one half the distance between the point from which the penalty is applied and that goal line.

front: What are the exceptions to the rule that a yardage penalty within 30 yards of the goal line cannot exceed half the distance to the goal line? Rule 8 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: Exceptions include pass interference; double penalties involving UR (Unnecessary Roughness) or RP (Rough Play), including those part of a dual penalty; and Unnecessary Roughness and Rough Play.

front: What is the closest to the goal line that the ball can be scrimmaged? Rule 8 | Section 3 | Article 1
back: The ball shall not be scrimmaged within the 1 yard (1 metre) line.

front: Under what condition is a first down awarded when a restricted penalty would have otherwise resulted in distance gained or the goal line reached? Rule 8 | Section 3 | Article 2
back: A first down shall be awarded if an unrestricted penalty would have resulted in distance gained, or the goal line reached by Team A.

front: What is the penalty if Team A commits an infraction when the PLS (Point of Last Scrimmage) is the A 1-yard line? Rule 8 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: The penalty is 1.2D – LD (Loss of Down on 1st or 2nd Down), 3D – DR (Down Repeated on 3rd Down).

front: What is the penalty if Team B commits an infraction when the PLS (Point of Last Scrimmage) is the B 1-yard line? Rule 8 | Section 3 | Article 3
back: The penalty is a 1st Down at the 1 yard (1 metre) line to Team A.

front: When Team A commits a foul in its own end zone while in possession of the ball, what is the outcome for Team B? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 1 a) 1.
back: Team B shall be awarded a rouge or a safety touch (1 or 2 points) as applicable, or option.

front: If Team A makes an offside pass in its own end zone and retains possession, what is awarded to Team B? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 1 a) 2.
back: Team B shall be awarded a rouge or a safety touch (1 or 2 points) as applicable, or option.

front: What is the outcome if a kicked ball is loose in the end zone before possession by Team A, and Team A commits a foul in its own end zone? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 1 a) 3.
back: Team B shall be awarded a rouge (1 point) or option.

front: What are Team B's options if an A player fumbles in their own end zone, and while the ball is loose, Team A commits illegal interference preventing Team B from gaining possession? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 1 a) 4.
back: Team B may accept a rouge or a safety touch (1 or 2 points) as applicable, or Team B may take possession of the ball as 1st down at the PLS or the 10 yard (10 metre) line, whichever is closer to the goal line.

front: What is awarded to Team A if Team B commits a foul in its own end zone while in possession of the ball? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 1 b) 1.
back: Team A shall be awarded a rouge or safety touch (1 or 2 points) as applicable.

front: If Team B makes an offside pass in its own end zone after receiving a Team A kick, what is awarded to Team A? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 1 b) 2.
back: Team A shall be awarded a rouge, or option.

front: What happens if Team B makes an offside pass in its own end zone while intercepting or after intercepting a Team A forward pass, and the ball goes dead in the end zone? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 1 b) 3.
back: There is no score. Team B shall scrimmage at the B 20.

front: What happens if Team B makes an offside pass in its own end zone while intercepting or after intercepting a Team A forward pass, and the ball goes dead in the field of play? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 1 b) 3.
back: There is no score. Team B shall scrimmage at the PBD or at the B 20 at the option of Team A.

front: What is the outcome if a kicked ball is loose in the Team B end zone before possession, and Team B commits a foul? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 1 b) 4.
back: Team A shall be awarded a rouge (1 point) or option.

front: What are Team A's penalty options if the ball is loose in the Team B end zone and Team B commits illegal interference preventing Team A from gaining possession? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 1 b) 5.
back: Team A may take possession of the ball as 1st down at the B 10, or at the PLS whichever is closer to the B goal line, or accept any score if Team A recovers the ball, or accept a score of 1 or 2 points as applicable and B will put the ball into play, or decline the penalty and allow Team B to scrimmage at the PBD if B advances the ball into the field of play.

front: How is a foul committed by Team A in the Team B end zone on a play from scrimmage penalized? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 2 a) 1.
back: The penalty shall be applied as though the foul has occurred on the field of play.

front: How is a 'restraining zone' foul by the kicking team in the receiving team's end zone penalized? Rule 8 | Section 4 | Article 2 a) 2.
